text:
You’ve probably seen the trend a hundred times before: a quick hook on screen reading, “When he says he wants kids,” accompanied by a playful tune. But every time this particular video pops up on my feed, I can’t help but pause and rewatch it.

It starts simple enough. A couple stands in the center of their kitchen. The mom is cradling newborn twins in her arms, and the dad is holding a sleepy toddler over his shoulder. You think, “Okay, that’s already a full house.” But then the wave begins. One by one, older kids stream past the camera—high-fiving their dad, waving, striking silly poses, riding a toy car, and scattering laughter across the room. By the time the video ends, you’ve counted a small army of children, and the sheer energy of the room hits you like a warm tidal wave.

On the surface, it’s a brilliant piece of bite-sized internet comedy. It subverts the expectation of a quiet, picturesque family unit and turns it into an overwhelming, hilarious flex of chaos. But if you look a little deeper, the video captures something far richer about modern parenthood, choice, and love that rarely gets talked about in our hyper-curated online world.

We live in a culture that often views children through a lens of anxiety and calculation. We talk about the financial cost of raising a child, the sacrifice of personal freedom, the loss of sleep, and the endless logistics of managing a household. And none of those concerns are wrong—parenting in the modern era is demanding, and raising a large family in today's economic climate feels almost radical. Yet, watching this family move together in their kitchen offers a striking counter-narrative.

Notice the details in those 26 seconds. The father isn't overwhelmed; he’s standing there with a calm, proud smile, casually high-fiving his kids as they parade past. The mother isn't panicked; she’s laughing, looking at her husband with an expression that says, “Look at what we built.” The children aren't chaotic in a disruptive way; they are joyful, expressive, and visibly comfortable in their own skin. The kitchen isn't a sterile showroom from an interior design magazine—it’s a lived-in sanctuary where life actually happens.

What strikes me most is how this video redefines abundance. In a world that constantly encourages us to accumulate material things—bigger cars, newer phones, higher titles—this family shows a completely different form of wealth. Their wealth is measured in shared laughter, chaotic mornings, built-in best friends, and a home overflowing with human connection. When that father said he wanted kids, he wasn't just asking for a baby; he was asking for a community, a legacy, and a life rich in shared experiences.

Of course, nobody is pretending that raising this many children is easy. Behind this lighthearted 26-second clip are thousands of hours of unpaid labor, endless laundry, chaotic meal preps, and moments of sheer exhaustion. But what the video captures so beautifully is the payoff. It reminds us that joy in life rarely comes from absolute control or quiet perfection. More often than not, joy lives inside the messy, unpredictable, and crowded spaces where people truly love one another.

So when the caption asks what happens “when he says he wants kids,” the video’s answer isn't a warning—it’s a celebration. It’s a reminder that choosing to bring life into the world, in whatever capacity feels right for you, is ultimately an act of immense hope. It’s choosing noise over silence, connection over isolation, and a full heart over a quiet house.

Whether you dream of having one child, a house full of six or seven, or none at all, there’s something undeniably beautiful about witnessing a family that leans so wholeheartedly into their chosen life. It’s a tiny, heartwarming reminder that the best things in life aren't things at all—they’re the people standing in the kitchen with you, making noise and high-fiving you as they walk by.

The death toll from catastrophic flash floods in Nepal has risen to 675, and 2,500 people remain missing, including 90 Americans. The sound of helicopters looking for survivors. So far, more than 7,500 people have been located. Rescuers.. struggling to reach devastated communities along the Nepal-Tibet border. The scale of the disaster finally coming into view four days after so much water, ice and debris swept through Himalayan valleys. Hundreds of homes, cars and bridges were instantly destroyed. Emergency teams from around the world have descended on the area to help. U-N Spokesman Stephane Dujarric:: “Humanitarians are moving at speed to save lives with OCHA and partners from the World Health Organization, the World Food Program, and various assisting national authorities in Nepal to deliver urgent life saving support. ”
Families continue to wait for news about their relatives, and fears of further flooding have hampered rescue efforts.

NewsNation's Laura Ingle:: “In a statement, the Ukrainian president Zelensky says a warehouse was struck followed by a detonation. Local military officials say at least 50 residential buildings were damaged in this attack, also causing a large fire spreading to other homes and a restaurant. President Zelinsky said he would punish the individuals who allowed explosive materials storage so close to homes, which is illegal.

I love it when I'm able to uncover a very specific Texas history  factoid that coincides with a Texas musical moment. It was 91 years ago today, on August 29, 1935, that Bob Wills heard Al  Stricklin playing with the Hi-Flyers at Fort Worth’s Cinderella Roof and offered him $30 a week to join the Texas Playboys. Stricklin became the first real pianist Wills had employed, and his jazz-influenced improvisational style essentially established the piano vocabulary of western swing. He played on more than 200 Wills recordings, including “New San Antonio Rose,” “Steel Guitar Rag,” and  this song, “Take Me Back to Tulsa.”

Stricklin left in May 1942 as World War II disrupted the band, taking a defense-industry job with North American Aircraft. He later occasionally played with Wills again in the 1950s and ’60s and returned for Wills’s famous final recording sessions in 1973.

text:
Effective coaching is built on a two-way relationship.

The best coaches understand that not every coaching relationship is meant to work. 

Sometimes the client needs guidance or expertise the coach does not have to offer. Sometimes the coach needs a level of commitment, honesty, or effort that the client is not ready to provide.

Great coaching is not about forcing a match. It is about finding alignment. 

The most meaningful change happens when the needs of the client and the strengths of the coach fit together in a positive and trusting way.

When both people are committed to learning, growth, and honest communication, coaching becomes far more than advice. It becomes a partnership focused on helping another human being become the person they want to become.

Life is good.
Marshall

text:
I exited Grace Holloway’s room and quickly scanned my surroundings for incoming threats. All clear. Before I can proceed further, I received a radio transmission from the woman in question:

“You had me under a gun…yet you just walked away? No monster alive turns the other cheek. No monster does that. A thinking man does that,” she said.

That caused me to pause and think…Hehehe.

When I had entered this city, Sofia trapped me and Sinclair under a city wide-lockdown. The only way out of the city was to retrieve the over-riding key from the governor of the city, Grace Holloway. The problem was two-fold:

1) She was taking orders from the collectivist tyrant herself.

2) Grace resented me and held me responsible for the kidnapping and enslavement of Eleanor Lamb. A ridiculous notion, since I had no control over that whole situation.

Regardless, Grace attempted to kill me many times in this city. Including when I was escorting the two Little Sisters when they were retrieving the Adam for me. Grace had sent Slicers to stop me from retrieving the Adam, failing to realize that had those slicers succeeded in putting me down, they would have harvested the Adam for themselves, killing the two innocent girls in the process. So Grace had put the lives of the innocent in danger.

I took all of that into account when I finally confronted Grace. She knew why I was there and offered me both the key and her life, saying.

“Go ahead. Do what you monsters always do,” she said, eyes full of fear, hatred and resignation.

Sinclair had chimed in and said: “The choice is yours. She is unarmed, for what it is worth.”

Objectively speaking, Grace had forfeited her right to live when she initiated conflict with me, intending to murder me, and almost got the Little Sisters killed indirectly. I would have been justified in executing her.

Instead, I just grabbed the key and walked away for two reasons:

1) She was no longer a threat.

2) She revealed that I had wounded her the last time we met ten years ago. She had tried to hug Eleanor, who was a ghoul at the time, and I smacked her in the face, breaking her jaw.

I have no recollection of ever doing that, but it would not surprise me if I did. Especially since I was ruled by the programming forced on me.

Which leads me to this question: How am I able to think and make decisions now? What changed in ten years? Did Eleanor played a hand in it?

I shook my head a little, readied my Rivet Gun, and kept moving. I have a feeling that I will get my answers when I reach Fountaine Futuristics, where Eleanor is being kept.

text:
The Big Sister goes down at last. I breathed heavily as I lowered my Rivet Gun. I did not realize how intimidating those machines can get.

When I released the Little Sister earlier from her Adam-induced madness, it was roughly an hour before I realized that I was being hunted. First, I spotted my hunter outside the glass wall in the ocean, looking at me with hatred and then swimming away. I knew then trouble was coming my way.

I was on edge from then on. No noise. No music. Only the sound of my footsteps and breathing. Almost like if the environment was being quiet because a predator was nearby. That did not do my nerves any favors.

Later, when I was moving through a corridor full of tv screens, I heard an ear-piercing scream, which caused the tv screens to shatter.  She sounded really mad. I double checked my weapons before I moved forward to confront her.

When we eventually met, it became a tense game of cat and mouse, with me being the mouse. Remembering what happened to me the last time, I maintained my distance from her and kept shooting at her. While she was chasing me, she kept throwing flames and objects my way. She was relentless, but I did not give her a chance to get close. Five minutes later, my strategy paid off. 

While I reloaded my weapons, I received a radio transmission from Sinclair:

“Holy Moses, son! Not even a Big Sister can keep you down! Well, come on back and melt the ice, an’ we can say goodbye to this two-bit ride.”

Gladly, Sinclair. Gladly.

Starbucks Workers Are Calling for a Nationwide Boycott
ByJenny Brown
Hoping  to pressure Starbucks to finally sign a contract with its 12,000  unionized baristas, Starbucks Workers United has called for a boycott of  the company. It is asking individuals as well as organizations and  unions to stop patronizing the coffee giant.

📷After  their largest and longest strike yet last November, unionized Starbucks  workers say the company seemed ready to bargain for a moment, but then  went back to stonewalling. The union is now calling for a nationwide  boycott to turn up the heat. (Timothy A. Clary / AFP via Getty Images)

No contract? No Starbucks coffee at the union hall.
Seeking  to pressure Starbucks to finally sign a contract with its 12,000  unionized baristas, Starbucks Workers United announced a boycott of the  chain August 25. In addition to individual customers, they are asking  organizations and unions to stop patronizing the coffee giant, including avoiding catering and sponsorships, until they get a contract.
The AFL-CIO has already signed on, and the 25,000-strong Chicago Teachers Union voted to boycott on August 26.
Starbucks  Workers United members conducted their largest and longest strike yet  last November, demanding that the company resolve its 550 unfair labor  practice charges and negotiate in good faith. Three thousand baristas in  one hundred cities struck, in some cases staying out into January. They  asked customers to delete their Starbucks phone app and avoid  patronizing all stores.
The company  seemed ready to bargain for a moment, but then went back to  stonewalling, baristas said. “They will continue to stonewall and stall  for as long as they believe they can get away with it,” said Campbell  Marusa, a five-year barista in Greeley, Colorado.
Sporadic  strikes have continued. August 15–16, workers in California, Missouri,  Tennessee, and Pennsylvania walked off the job. The walkouts came during  Unicorn Frappuccino weekend, when the stores briefly offered a  complicated multicolored drink that spiked sales and exhausted workers.  Baristas were told they had to work that weekend and could not take time  except for emergencies.

In  Nashville, baristas walked off August 15 to raise the alarm about a new  blending powder the company rolled out in mid-July that became easily  airborne and was giving workers sore throats, coughs, and headaches from  breathing it.

Starbucks baristas have  been fighting for a first contract for nearly five years. Workers  started an organizing wave with union election wins in Buffalo, New  York, in late 2021. Since then, over 700 stores have voted union —  affiliating with the Service Employees International Union’s Workers  United division — but that’s still fewer than 5 percent of the company’s  16,000 outlets in the United States.

To  stop the union’s spread, the company has racked up the largest number of  unfair labor practices in US history, with 550 still unresolved.  Despite well-documented management intimidation, the union continues to  grow by several stores a month.

Three at All Times
A key contract demand is around understaffing. Workers are demanding  three people on the floor at all times, and they want available hours to  go to current baristas, rather than the company’s prevailing practice  of hiring more people and keeping established workers starved for hours.Striking Nashville barista Baylor Baucom told the Nashville Banner that his store sometimes has only two workers. “That’s unacceptable, in  my opinion, considering how many different positions we have on our  floor — making drinks, making the food, taking orders, taking orders in  the drive-through.”Many longer-term  baristas report that staffing has worsened in the last five years. “The  working conditions and food service are getting worse while prices are  getting higher,” said Marusa. Many workers report that even when they  are available to work more, managers keep their hours below the number  required to receive benefits.Marusa said  a coworker in Greeley keeps asking for more hours but is being kept at  the minimum. “After asking the manager for more hours, my store manager  told her that there are resources to help her budget her money,” said  Marusa. “With the hours that she’s getting scheduled, she’s getting paid  less than $800 a month. The issue isn’t how she’s budgeting her money;  the issue is that she is being chronically underscheduled.”Pay  has improved since the union started organizing, but in forty-three  states the starting wages are still below $16. The union is asking for  $17 an hour starting pay and 4 percent annual raises.

Grueling Pace, Angry Customers
Because  there is not enough staff for the workload, baristas say they are  forced to speed up their work to a grueling pace, while customers face  long wait times. Customer frustration is absorbed by the workers.“Everyone  in my store was being scheduled less than their stated preferred hours  because of our ‘labor budget,’” said Marusa. Because of this, workers  can’t take sick time, lest they drop below the required hours limit.When  a coworker was shoved and stomped by a customer in June, she had to go  to the hospital, Marusa said. “Her ribs were bruised, but she came into  work the next day.” She couldn’t take time off because she would lose  precious hours and risk being fired, said Marusa.The  workers want health and safety addressed in the contract, including  procedures to protect against assaults by customers. More robust  staffing would make attacks less likely, they said.“It honestly affects your mental health sometimes,” Baucom told the Banner,  “because you’re understaffed, you’re being told that you need to go  faster, and then you turn around and a customer is yelling at you  because they’ve been waiting too long.”Another  sticking point is the annoying requirement to write something cheery  and spontaneous on each cup. Workers face discipline if they don’t do  it. One wrote on Reddit that they had been fired for “not including  required markings on cups put in handoff plane.” Another responded,  “Nothing irks me more when I’m running a shift and I have a callout, I’m  supporting on bar and I’m running around doing a million things and my  manager approaches me and says ‘there should be no excuses for not  writing on cups.’”

“Inhaling Drywall Dust”
The union chalked a win in mid-August when Starbucks withdrew its new Blending Powder Beverage Mix, used in cold “refresher” drinks,  that was making many baristas sick with respiratory symptoms. Many took  to social media with their reactions to the powder.The  union asked an occupational health professor at the University of  Illinois Medical Center, Peter Orris, to evaluate the powder’s  ingredients. He found that three of them — gum arabic, xanthan gum, and amorphous silica —  are associated with respiratory issues when inhaled. He recommended  masking, special ventilation, and special cleanup procedures to handle  the product. Workers who have reactions should avoid the product, he  wrote.Baristas took to social media to  celebrate the product’s withdrawal, commenting “No more inhaling drywall  dust!!” and “I can finally breathe on cold bar again,” and “Thank the  lord, my asthma was tweaking. . . .  It was effecting me so bad but I  felt weird saying anything about it at work.”“We  need to turn up the pressure,” said Marusa, citing the boycott. She  encouraged unions and other organizations to pass a resolution to run “a  Starbucks-free organization [and] encourage your community members to boycott Starbucks.”

Heavenly Father, Almighty God, Creator of heaven and earth, we come before You with heavy hearts in the wake of this sudden tragedy in Fort Collins. We pray for Your deep comfort to rest upon the grieving family and loved ones of the person who tragically lost their life. Lord, wrap them in Your peace that surpasses all understanding, and be their refuge and strength in this hour of unbearable sorrow.

We lift up the five individuals who were injured on West Mountain Avenue. Lord Jesus, You are the Great Physician; we ask that You guide the hands of the medical teams caring for them, ease their pain, and grant them full and swift healing in body, mind, and spirit. Bring calm and supernatural strength to their families as they wait by hospital bedsides.

Father, a tragic moment like this reminds us of the fragility of human life and the uncertainty of our time on this earth. Scripture tells us that You so loved the world that You gave Your only begotten Son, Jesus Christ, so that whoever believes in Him shall not perish but have everlasting life. We pray that amidst this darkness, Your light shines brightly. Open hearts to the message of salvation—that through faith in Jesus Christ, who bore our sins on the cross and rose again, we are offered forgiveness, hope, and eternal life with You. May those who do not know You discover the unshakeable assurance of Your grace today.

Grant wisdom, endurance, and compassion to the first responders, police officers, and grief counselors ministering to the Fort Collins community. Unify the residents and festival-goers in love, support, and care for one another as they walk through the aftermath of this heartbreak.

We place our trust, our lives, and our eternal hope in Your hands, praying all these things in the precious and mighty name of Jesus Christ, our Savior.  Amen.

text:
My Position on National Socialism

I am neither a National Socialist nor interested in pretending National Socialism provides a permanent answer to the crisis of Western civilisation.

I understand why it attracts people during periods of national humiliation, demographic anxiety, institutional collapse and social fragmentation. It offers certainty where liberalism offers ambiguity, collective purpose where individualism produces atomisation, and mobilisation where parliamentary politics can appear incapable of decisive action.

That can impose order upon chaos.

But imposing order and building civilisation are not the same thing.

National Socialism may provide a temporary answer to certain symptoms of national decline because an authoritarian state possesses enormous power to mobilise resources, direct institutions and enforce objectives.

My objection is what happens afterwards.

A civilisation cannot permanently exist in a state of political mobilisation. Eventually emergency government must become ordinary government. Revolutionary energy must become institutions. Mobilisation must become inheritance. Political authority must become stewardship.

This is where National Socialism fails my philosophical test.

I reject socialism regardless of whether it arrives carrying a red flag or wrapped in the national flag.

The economy should serve civilisation, but that does not mean the state should absorb the organic institutions between the individual and government.

Family. Church. Guild. Community. Property.

These should possess genuine authority of their own.

My conception of civilisation therefore runs against totalitarian politics.

I want authority distributed through an ordered hierarchy of institutions, beginning with the household and extending outward through community and nation.

The state should defend that order.

It should not become that order.

National Socialism also attempted to answer questions of belonging through an excessively racial conception of civilisation. Ancestry matters. Peoplehood matters. Historical continuity matters. But civilisation cannot be reduced to biology.

Civilisation is also inheritance, memory, language, law, architecture, religion, custom and obligation.

For Britain especially, Christianity cannot become an instrument subordinate to racial politics or the state.

God stands above political authority.

The state therefore cannot be absolute.

Authority must answer to something higher than itself.

I understand National Socialism historically as something that becomes attractive when a civilisation believes ordinary politics has become incapable of saving it.

But emergency mobilisation is not a philosophy for a thousand years.

Civilisation requires institutions capable of surviving mediocre rulers, families capable of transmitting culture without instruction from government, communities capable of governing themselves, property sufficiently distributed to create independence, and leaders who understand themselves as custodians rather than owners of the nation.

My answer to liberal modernity therefore isn’t National Socialism.

It is stewardship.

Not the isolated individual.

Not the omnipotent state.

But an ordered civilisation of household, community, faith and nation, each possessing responsibilities appropriate to its sphere.

National Socialism can mobilise a population.

My concern is building a civilisation that does not permanently require mobilisation in order to survive.

That is the difference between political reaction and civilisational restoration.

text:
The Sullivan brothers were five brothers from Waterloo who served together in the U.S. Navy during World War II. 

Their deaths aboard the USS Juneau (CL-52) became one of the most tragic family losses of the war.

George, Francis, Joseph, Madison, and Albert Sullivan insisted on serving together after the United States entered the war following the Attack on Pearl Harbor. The Navy honored their request, assigning all five brothers to the USS Juneau.

On November 13, 1942, during the Naval Battle of Guadalcanal, the Juneau was heavily damaged before being struck by a Japanese torpedo that caused the ship to explode and sink. 

Most of the crew perished in the blast or while awaiting rescue.

Although George Sullivan initially survived the sinking, rescue efforts were delayed for several days. 

Exhaustion, dehydration, exposure, and shark-infested waters claimed the lives of most survivors, and George also died before help arrived.

The loss of all five brothers deeply affected the nation and prompted changes in U.S. military policy regarding the assignment of close family members to the same unit. 

Their parents later traveled the country promoting war bonds, and Franklin D. Roosevelt personally offered his condolences. https://t.co/GhZF95qvfE

text:
Jasmine Crockett is not the Negro wrangler.

Let me repeat that: Jasmine Crockett is NOT the Negro wrangler.

Jasmine Crockett and James Talarico had a primary. Jasmine lost. The very next day, she endorsed him and made clear that she would support the Democratic nominee.

Y’all do not get to dictate what that support has to look like.

Jasmine has chosen to spend her time helping down-ballot Democrats. And guess what? That helps Talarico too. Increasing Democratic turnout in local races increases the number of voters moving through the ballot in November. The government closest to the people matters, and organizing those voters strengthens the entire ticket.

But here is where I have a problem.

Between the Democratic primary and the Republican runoff, Talarico and his campaign had a window to study the map.

Where was he weak?

Where was Jasmine strong?

Which communities overwhelmingly supported her but did not support him?

Then he should have gone there.

He should have spent those months in those communities meeting Black voters, pastors, local elected officials, organizers, business owners, community leaders and influencers. He should have been listening, building relationships and creating his own coalition for the general election.

If that work was not done, that is not Jasmine Crockett’s failure.

And now, months into the general election, people are worried about whether Talarico can generate the VOLUME of Black turnout necessary to win Texas.

Volume matters.

Getting roughly 85 percent of 200,000 Black voters is very different from getting roughly 85 percent of 1.5 million Black voters.

You cannot take Black voters for granted during the coalition-building phase and then decide the most prominent Black political figure in the state needs to go round everybody up when you need turnout.

Black voters can see exactly what that is.

And even if Jasmine decided tomorrow to campaign beside him everywhere he needs help, voters are still capable of asking the obvious question:

Where was HE?

Where was James Talarico when there was no emergency? Where was his campaign when there was time to listen instead of ask? Where was the investment in communities Jasmine had already demonstrated could be mobilized?

A surrogate can open a door.

A surrogate cannot build your relationship with an electorate for you.

So stop putting the responsibility for Black turnout on Jasmine Crockett.

Blame the candidate. Blame the campaign. Blame the consultants. Blame whoever looked at the primary results and failed to spend the following months building relationships in the communities necessary to create the turnout they now need.

Jasmine Crockett endorsed the nominee.

She is supporting Democrats.

She is doing her job.

She is not the Negro wrangler.

Leave Black people alone.

text:
Executive Assessment
Antifa is best understood as a decentralized militant political ecosystem rather than a conventional national organization. It has no single headquarters, recognized commander, universal membership roll or binding chain of command. Its cohesion comes from shared ideology, symbols, tactics, enemies, digital infrastructure and a belief that direct action - including force in some circumstances - is legitimate against people or institutions labeled fascist, racist or authoritarian.

CURRENT FBI OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION
The FBI's current posture is significantly stronger than its 2020 description. In December 2025, Michael Glasheen, operations director of the FBI National Security Branch, told Congress that antifa was the Bureau's 'primary concern' and 'the most immediate violent threat that we're facing.' Current FBI and Justice Department releases also use the term 'Antifa Cell' for the North Texas network convicted in the Prairieland ICE facility attack. This is an operational threat assessment focused on violent actors and cells. It does not make anti-fascist belief, peaceful protest or political dissent a federal crime.

The structural problem remains important. Antifa can be simultaneously an ideology, a movement and a label adopted by identifiable local groups. The absence of a national command structure does not prevent small cells from planning violence. It does, however, make claims of a single nationwide conspiracy difficult to prove unless investigators can establish communications, financing, direction or material support connecting separate actors.
The record supports two conclusions that are often treated as mutually exclusive. First, it is unsupported to claim that a centralized antifa command directed every riot associated with the 2020 unrest. Second, it is equally misleading to describe antifa as nothing more than an abstract idea. Local collectives, recurring tactics, organized black-bloc formations, doxxing networks and violent offenders have existed under the antifa banner.
What Antifa Is
The term is a shortened form of anti-fascist. In its broadest meaning, it can describe anyone who opposes fascism. In its modern militant usage, however, antifa refers to a decentralized current of revolutionary left-wing activism that favors direct action over reliance on elections, courts or conventional institutions.
American adherents have included anarchists, communists, socialists and other radical left activists. Not everyone using the label accepts violence, and not every person who confronts a white supremacist is antifa. The security concern arises from individuals and cells that treat physical coercion as legitimate political action.

THE OPERATING DOCTRINE
Militant adherents commonly describe confrontation as preemptive self-defense: fascist movements, they argue, must be denied public space before they can recruit and acquire power. Critics describe the same method as political street violence because activists decide who qualifies as fascist and then use intimidation or force without legal authority. Different cells and different nights can fit either description, but violence remains violence regardless of the justification claimed.

Origins: Before the American Movement
1921  |  Arditi del Popolo - Italy
Former soldiers, workers, anarchists, communists and socialists formed Arditi del Popolo to resist Benito Mussolini's Blackshirts. It was an early organized example of militant anti-fascist street defense. Modern antifa cites this tradition as ancestry, although there is no continuous organizational line from the Italian formation to contemporary American cells.
1932  |  Antifaschistische Aktion - Germany
The Communist Party of Germany launched Antifaschistische Aktion during the final crisis of the Weimar Republic. Its two-flag imagery became the visual ancestor of today's antifa logo. The history is politically complicated: the Communist Party also attacked social democrats as 'social fascists,' demonstrating that the movement's concept of fascism could extend beyond actual Nazi organizations to competing forces on the left.
October 4, 1936  |  The Battle of Cable Street - London
Anti-fascists, Jewish residents, trade unionists, communists and local communities blocked a march by Oswald Mosley's British Union of Fascists. Cable Street became a lasting model for the principle that fascist mobilization should be physically denied access to public space.
1946-1950  |  The 43 Group - Britain
Mostly Jewish veterans of the Second World War organized to disrupt postwar fascist meetings associated with Mosley. Members used surveillance, infiltration and physical confrontation. The group reinforced the militant tradition that state institutions could not always be trusted to stop fascist organizing.
1970s-1980s  |  Punk scenes, skinheads and Anti-Fascist Action
Neo-Nazi recruitment inside British and European music scenes produced organized anti-fascist resistance. Anti-Fascist Action formed in Britain in 1985 and embraced direct confrontation as well as political organizing. This era established many of the cultural and tactical patterns later adopted in the United States.
 
The American Lineage
1987  |  The Baldies and Anti-Racist Action - Minneapolis
The Baldies emerged from the Minneapolis punk scene to confront neo-Nazi skinheads. Members helped build Anti-Racist Action, the clearest American precursor to modern antifa. Its strategy was often summarized as denying racist organizations space to meet, recruit or operate, including through physical confrontation.

2007  |  Rose City Antifa - Portland
Rose City Antifa formed after efforts to shut down a neo-Nazi skinhead music festival. It is generally identified as the oldest continuously named American antifa collective. Portland's political culture, recurring far-right rallies and willingness of opposing groups to fight in public made the city the movement's most visible American arena.

The Recurring Tactical System
Black bloc is not a permanent organization. It is a protest tactic in which participants wear similar black clothing and conceal their identities. The uniform appearance complicates identification, allows individuals to move through a crowd and can prevent police or journalists from connecting a specific person to a particular act.

Doxxing involves collecting and publishing personal information about targeted individuals. Antifa collectives have used it to identify alleged extremists, contact employers, pressure venues and expose private associations. Some investigations have documented genuine extremists. Other campaigns have created risks of misidentification, harassment and punishment without due process.

Deplatforming seeks to deny speakers, organizations and political opponents access to campuses, meeting halls, payment systems and online services. Peaceful advocacy for cancellation is protected expression. Threats, assault, arson or property destruction used to force cancellation cross into criminal conduct.
Street confrontation can include shields, helmets, clubs, chemical sprays, fireworks and coordinated movement. In more serious cases, individuals associated with militant anti-fascist or anarchist networks have used incendiaries, improvised explosives and firearms. These high-end attacks remain a minority of total anti-fascist activism, but they define the domestic-security concern.

2017: The National Emergence
January 20, 2017  |  Presidential inauguration - Washington, D.C.
Black-bloc militants smashed storefronts, damaged automated teller machines and burned a limousine during protests surrounding President Trump's inauguration. The episode pushed the word antifa into national American coverage.

February 1, 2017  |  University of California, Berkeley
Masked militants used fires, property destruction and assaults during the successful effort to stop a Milo Yiannopoulos appearance. The event became a defining example of speech being canceled through coercion rather than defeated through argument.

April 15, 2017  |  Berkeley street battle
Antifa counter-demonstrators and right-wing activists fought in a prolonged confrontation that produced injuries and arrests. Similar events increasingly operated less like protests and more like rival groups preparing for physical combat.

August 11-12, 2017  |  Charlottesville
The Unite the Right rally brought white supremacists, neo-Nazis and counter-protesters into violent confrontation. Neo-Nazi James Alex Fields Jr. murdered Heather Heyer by driving a car into a crowd. Antifa participants were involved in street fighting, but antifa did not kill Heyer. Both facts are necessary for an honest record.

2019: Violence and Escalation
In Portland, journalist Andy Ngo was beaten during clashes involving black-clad militants and was hospitalized. In a separate event, Willem van Spronsen attacked an Immigration and Customs Enforcement contractor facility in Tacoma with incendiary devices and was killed by police. Van Spronsen's own writings aligned him with militant anti-fascist and anarchist causes.
 
2020: Maximum Visibility
After George Floyd's death, millions of Americans participated in peaceful demonstrations. It is false to label those demonstrators collectively as antifa, and federal field assessments did not establish that a national antifa command directed the unrest.
It is also false to erase the militant component. Portland experienced more than 90 consecutive nights of demonstrations. Federal prosecutions included assault, arson, attempted arson and destruction of government property. After larger peaceful gatherings ended on many nights, smaller groups repeatedly targeted the federal courthouse with fireworks, lasers, incendiary devices and attempts to breach defensive barriers.
Seattle's Capitol Hill Organized Protest zone demonstrated the danger of collapsing public authority, although it should not be treated as an antifa headquarters. Mixed activists occupied the area, and two people were killed in separate shootings inside or near the zone. The deaths do not establish that antifa ordered the shootings, but they reveal the security consequences of an unaccountable autonomous space.

August 29, 2020  |  The killing of Aaron Danielson - Portland
Michael Reinoehl, who publicly described himself as '100 percent antifa,' shot and killed Patriot Prayer supporter Aaron Danielson after street confrontations. Reinoehl said he acted to protect another person. Police obtained an arrest warrant, but he was killed by a federal fugitive task force before the homicide case could be tried. This remains the clearest American homicide associated with a self-described antifa activist during the period.

WHAT THE 2020 RECORD PROVES
The unrest contained peaceful protesters, criminals, opportunists, organized militants and people with no antifa affiliation. The evidence does not support one national antifa command directing every city. It does support the presence of antifa-aligned individuals, black-bloc formations and violent anarchist tactics within some of the most destructive episodes.

Why Antifa Appeared to Disappear
The mass-street phase declined after 2020. Public fatigue increased, prosecutions accumulated, cameras became more pervasive and large formations produced extensive evidence for investigators. The antifa label also became politically toxic and operationally expensive.
The response was adaptation rather than necessarily dissolution. Smaller direct-action groups could organize around a specific target without maintaining a famous brand. Temporary coalitions, encrypted communications and issue-based names offered more protection than a permanent antifa identity. Digital exposure campaigns and targeted vandalism attracted less attention than nightly street formations.
This is what 'went dark' means in analytical terms. It does not prove that every anonymous left-wing crime is antifa. It means the incentives shifted away from public branding and toward small cells, compartmented communications and actions claimed under temporary names - or not claimed at all.

2025: The Federal Strategy Changes
September 22, 2025  |  Presidential designation
President Trump signed an executive order designating antifa a domestic terrorist organization and directing federal agencies to investigate illegal operations, financing and support associated with people acting in its name.

September 25, 2025  |  NSPM-7
A national security presidential memorandum directed agencies to counter organized political violence through investigation of participants, networks, financial support and institutional assistance. The operational focus moved from controlling crowds to identifying conspiracies and support systems.

THE LEGAL LIMIT
The United States does not have a domestic designation system identical to the statutory Foreign Terrorist Organization list. A presidential label does not by itself criminalize association, political belief or peaceful advocacy. Prosecutors still need chargeable conduct such as conspiracy, assault, arson, stalking, attempted murder or material support tied to legally defined terrorism offenses.

November 2025  |  Foreign antifa-linked designations
The State Department used existing foreign-terrorism authorities to designate Antifa Ost in Germany, the Informal Anarchist Federation/International Revolutionary Front in Italy, and two Greek militant groups. These are distinct foreign organizations, not chapters of one American headquarters.
 
The Cases That Changed the Debate
July 4, 2025  |  Prairieland ICE facility - Alvarado, Texas
According to evidence presented in federal court, participants arrived with body armor, radios, firearms and materials for an organized attack. Cameras and vehicles were damaged, fireworks or explosives were used, and a responding Alvarado police officer was shot in the neck.
In March 2026, a federal jury convicted nine defendants. By July, 15 defendants had received combined sentences exceeding 556 years. Benjamin Hanil Song received a 100-year sentence for attempted murder and related offenses. The FBI and Justice Department explicitly described the network as a North Texas Antifa Cell.
The case did not prove the existence of a national antifa army. It proved something more precise: a localized cell operating beneath the broader ideological banner could coordinate political violence using weapons, protective equipment, communications and planned roles.

June 2026  |  Direct Action Minnesota indictment
Federal prosecutors charged 15 members and associates of Direct Action Minnesota with conspiracy to impede federal officers and related offenses during immigration-enforcement operations. Other counts included stalking, threats, assault and destruction of government property. These accusations remain allegations unless proved in court. Defense attorneys argue that the government is criminalizing dissent; prosecutors contend the defendants moved from protected advocacy into coordinated force.

Europe: A More Formal Militant Layer
European anti-fascist and anarchist militancy includes organizations with greater continuity and more deliberate attack patterns than most American street collectives. Germany's Antifa Ost, also called Hammerbande, was accused of planned assaults against people it labeled right-wing. The Informal Anarchist Federation and affiliated networks have claimed letter bombs and attacks on state, diplomatic and commercial targets. Greek militant cells have claimed explosive attacks on government and infrastructure targets.

These groups share anti-fascist, anti-capitalist or anti-state frames, but they should not be merged into a fictional international headquarters. Transnational overlap is more likely to appear through propaganda, digital hosting, tactical manuals, fundraising methods and imitation than through a single chain of command.

The Digital Infrastructure Question
The strategic contest has moved toward servers, encrypted channels, doxxing archives, claim-of-responsibility sites and instructional material. A digital service may host lawful political speech alongside content used by violent networks. That creates a difficult investigative boundary: authorities must identify criminal facilitation without treating privacy tools or radical speech as proof of terrorism.

The key intelligence questions are therefore specific. Who selected the target? Who provided money, transportation, weapons or technical assistance? Which participants knew violence was planned? Did a platform merely host content, or did administrators knowingly facilitate an attack? Those questions produce evidence. Broad ideological labels do not.

Decode Conflict Assessment
Antifa's strongest defense was always structural ambiguity. It could mobilize through recognizable symbols and tactics while denying the existence of an organization responsible for the consequences. That description was partially accurate: there was no single national headquarters. It was also incomplete: local groups and cells could still organize, train, identify targets and commit violence.

The current FBI no longer treats the issue primarily as a semantic argument over whether antifa is an organization. Its operational focus is on violent antifa-linked actors, identifiable cells and conspiracies. The North Texas convictions gave that approach a concrete legal foundation. The Minnesota case will further test how courts distinguish coordinated violence from protected monitoring and protest.

The movement's 2017-2020 street-army phase is no longer operating at the same scale. That does not establish disappearance. It indicates adaptation under pressure. The black uniform and public flag became liabilities once facial recognition, video analysis, conspiracy charges and financial investigations improved.

BOTTOM LINE
Antifa did not need a national headquarters to produce organized violence. It needed local trust, shared tactics, concealed identities and a political narrative that presented coercion as defense. The next violent cell may never display an antifa flag. Its lineage may emerge only through target selection, communications, digital infrastructure and the evidence recovered after arrests.

Evidence Standards
This assessment distinguishes established convictions from pending allegations. It does not attribute every act committed during racial-justice, anti-ICE or anti-government demonstrations to antifa. It also does not treat peaceful anti-fascist belief as criminal. Attribution should rest on self-identification, group records, communications, coordinated tactics, court evidence and official investigative findings.

text:
Werner Herzog on "The Wheels on the Bus":
(Sound of wind, perhaps a distant, discordant hum)

"Observe the bus. A hulking metal carcass, commandeered by an unseen, perhaps nonexistent, intelligence. Its wheels, they turn, 'round and 'round, with a mindless, algorithmic insistence. This, they tell us, is the vehicle of civilization, ferrying its passengers towards an ever-receding horizon of promised destinations.

But who, one must ask, truly grips the wheel? Who navigates by the stars of emotional truth, by the magnetic north of accountability? The answer, I suspect, is a void, an empty driver's seat. The passengers, lulled into a state of bovine placidity, sing their 'merry song.' A song of conformity, a childish rhyme to drown out the grinding of gears, the screech of metal against metal as the chassis strains. The music, you see, is so very loud, designed to obscure the silence from the driver's seat, to mask the chilling truth that this colossus, this societal omnibus, might possess no functioning brakes.

And so it hurtles onward, 'round and 'round, or perhaps, in a terrifyingly straight line towards a precipice only a few dare to acknowledge. The landscape outside is a blur of fleeting distractions. Inside, the song drones on, a mantra of oblivion. The wheels, indifferent to the fate of their cargo, simply continue their rotation, a perfect, mechanical metaphor for a journey undertaken without wisdom, careening towards a future shaped not by conscious design, but by the blind, idiot force of unexamined momentum. One day, the singing will abruptly cease. If emotional intelligence is not taught to fix the brakes then I imagine the view from the window wont matter much anymore if the brakes on the bus aren't fixed as soon as possible."

...

Werner Herzog on "The Itsy-Bitsy Spider":
(Sound of dripping water, a faint, skittering noise)

"And then, we have the arachnid. The 'Itsy-Bitsy Spider.' A creature of almost ludicrous fragility, attempting its ascent up the 'waterspout' – this, we are told, is the grand edifice of societal norms, the slick, vertical promise of promotions, of accumulating currency. The spider, driven by some primal, unarticulated yearning, perhaps what it dimly perceives as 'up,' begins its climb. It is a creature already bearing the weight of an unseen burden – its emotional suffering, a private, internal weeping.

But societal structures, much like the indifferent plumbing of the universe, are not designed for such delicate ascents. The 'rain,' you see, is not mere water. It is the rotting accumulation of unprocessed human suffering within a collective that has systematically failed to educate its smallest members in the language of the heart, in emotional intelligence. It is the downpour of a thousand unmourned griefs, a torrent of unspoken anxieties, and it washes the spider out, a predictable, almost banal tragedy.

Then, the 'sun' appears – the so-called 'help.' A course of medication, perhaps, designed to numb the fall. Or the therapist, offering a different 'tube' to climb. Society, with a benign, almost patronizing smile, gestures towards a new structure. Perhaps it is no longer the waterspout of raw commerce, but a 'metal pole' of 'wellness,' of 'self-improvement.' Yet, this new edifice, for all its gleaming surfaces, shares the same flaws as the old. The spider, still unversed in emotional literacy, still carrying its residual emotional pain, attempts the climb again, with almost the same vulnerabilities as before.

The cycle is complete, only to begin anew. The climb, the rain, the fall, the superficial drying, the redirection to another treacherous ascent. The spider, in its Sisyphean toil, becomes the individual ensnared in systems that offer the illusion of progress, while the core deficit – the profound, societal neglect of emotional understanding – ensures each climb is merely a prelude to the next fall. The spout changes; the suffering, and the ignorance that perpetuates it, remain."

text:
In Sibu, Sarawak, they don’t just burn paper money for Hungry Ghost Festival.
They build a ship.

This week at Fong Hwang San Ur Par Wang Kong Temple (凤凰山二霸王公庙), a 68-foot bamboo-and-paper vessel was set alight. Temple members spent weeks assembling it by hand — bamboo frame, paper skin, no metal. Then they burned it at night so the dead could sail.

The meaning is local and specific. Early Chinese settlers left Fujian and Guangdong, built a life on the Rajang, and never went home. 

When they died, their descendants burned a junk so those souls could still make the crossing. The same fire also feeds the “good brothers” — wandering ghosts with no one left to offer them anything.

After the ship goes, people rush the altar and grab the food. That’s 抢孤 — taking the blessing home.

This is not a tourism board reenactment. It’s a Foochow/Hokkien custom that crossed the South China Sea and stayed. One temple in Sibu still does the full ship. That is how diaspora culture actually survives: not as a museum label, but as weeks of unpaid labour and a night of fire.

Also for the overseas diaspora: 

中元节在砂拉越诗巫：凤凰山二霸王公庙烧了一艘近70尺的竹纸冥船。早期南来的祖先回不了唐山，后人就扎船、烧船，送他们过海。顺便超度没人祭的好兄弟。烧完抢孤。这才是活着的民间信仰，不是宣传片。

They're tools of survival, precision instruments of craft, and — for many — a daily companion that quietly gets the job done. The best knives aren't just functional; they're a reflection of the maker's art and the carrier's character.

Steel quality — CPM-154, S30V, and D2 are popular choices for their edge retention and corrosion resistance.

Blade geometry — Drop points for versatility, tanto for penetration, clip points for precision.

Handle ergonomics — G10, aluminum, and carbon fiber each offer a different feel and weight profile.

Locking mechanism — Frame locks, liner locks, and axis locks each have their strengths for EDC use.

text:
While performing an authorized Civic Service assignment, a volunteer acts as an agent of the jurisdiction for liability purposes and shall be defended and indemnified by the jurisdiction for lawful acts performed within the authorized scope of service.
>
> No indemnification applies to intentional misconduct, criminal conduct, gross negligence, reckless conduct, or work performed outside required licensing, training, or authorization.

**Competence gates.** Licensed trades require licensed people and pulled permits and real inspections, same as any contractor. Safety orientation before the first hour. Minors work only under the rules that already govern minors, with a guardian's consent and age-appropriate tasks. A volunteer may decline any assignment at any moment for any reason without penalty, and may walk off a site they judge unsafe.

Good faith gets protected. Recklessness does not.

---

## Section 7 — Interstate Civic Service Reciprocity

This is the part with real reach, and it is worth building carefully.

**The mechanism.** A jurisdiction that needs help posts a public request. Another state may sponsor its own residents and businesses to answer that request, and issues the tax credit against its own tax base for hours verified in the requesting jurisdiction.

The host gets the labor. The sponsor pays the credit. No cash grant, no federal middleman, no strings attached to the host's budget or policy.

**Why it works politically.** A legislature in a state with money can vote to help a state without money and never appropriate a dollar. They forgo revenue on labor their own citizens chose to donate. That is a smaller ask than a spending bill and a cleaner one, since not a cent moves through anybody's slush fund.

**Why it protects the poor state.** The host must ask. There is no crew arriving uninvited, no outside foundation deciding what a town needs, no condition attached about how the town governs itself. A request can be withdrawn. Sovereignty stays put.

**Required guardrails:**

- **Invitation only.** No sponsored crew enters without a posted, authorized request from the host's elected body or its emergency manager.
- **Host displacement certification.** The host certifies the work is additive under its own law, and no out-of-state crew may take work from a local contractor or a local worker.
- **Licensing.** Either the host grants temporary reciprocity by rule, or out-of-state trades work under the supervision of a locally licensed professional. Emergency licensing reciprocity is well-trodden ground; the Emergency Management Assistance Compact has moved licensed personnel across state lines for decades, and its architecture is worth copying rather than reinventing.
- **Coverage follows the volunteer.** The sponsoring state's coverage and the host's indemnity are both stated in writing before mobilization, and no crew rolls until that document exists.
- **Pool caps.** Each sponsoring state sets an annual out-of-state hour ceiling and publishes it.
- **No conditions.** A sponsoring state may not attach policy demands to a civic service offer. The day this becomes leverage is the day it should be shut down.

**On the Compact Clause.** Article I, Section 10 requires congressional consent for certain agreements between states. The Supreme Court has read that narrowly, requiring consent where a compact encroaches on federal supremacy. A reciprocity arrangement that only governs each state's own tax credits and its own volunteers probably does not need consent, and a formal multistate compact with a governing commission probably does. Get an opinion from counsel and, better yet, ask Congress for blanket consent up front under Section 11. Consent is cheap and litigation is not.

text:
It sounds like recognizing the way that the US was intentionally structured to begin with, which was destroyed by three things: Treaties; Interstate Commerce; the Spending Power. 

When the Revolutionary War ended, each colony was recognized by England as a separate nation, inheriting all the elements of sovereignty as the Crown has possessed. Together, these new states formed the "United States" through Articles of Confederation, which kept most of this sovereignty in tact. 

This didn't work well, so they figured, the true sovereigns are the People and they can split up the sovereignty any way they choose. The Constitution is a written document that places a limited amount of power on national issues with a federal government. 

The remainder of the powers, also called the "police" or municipal powers to protect general public health, safety and moral from substantial harm and to advance the general welfare in public works stayed with the states. [The meaning of "welfare" became expanded by a series of court cases.]

This system became known as "dual sovereignty." It is not a hierarchical system. It is supposed to occupy two separate orbits. Only when federal and state laws conflict, or the federal law fully "occupies the field" does the "Supremacy Clause" kick in and federal law prevails.

So, those things that "blurred the lines" from original intent: Treaties; Interstate Commerce; and the Spending Power?

Treaties were never supposed to give powers to the federal government that it was given in the Constitution. If the federal government did not have the power to implement some provision of a treaty, then the states were supposed to implement. That has not been the case and there are laws written every day by Congress where you cannot find the specific delegated authority to do so in Article I Clause 8 of the Constitution. 

Interstate Commerce started out as meaning to "make regular" commerce amongst the states. That meant the same weights and measures, the same currency, etc. It was stretched to mean the federal regulation of any thing that was involved in the stream of commerce between or among states - water, products, etc. [Huge breakdown of dual sovereignty.]

The "Spending Power" has allowed Congress to regulated anything it wants in the purview of the state's police powers. Justice O’Connor in New York v US 505 US 144 (1992) explained that: …the Constitution authorizes Congress …” to pay the Debts and provide for the… general Welfare of the United States” Article 1, Section 8, Clause 1.

From the Spending Power Congress could now create a conditional program on welfare or health (or Surface Mining and Reclamation for that matter) and offer it to the states. The program would be paid for by federal funds with a state (and small county) match and be administered by the states and counties. 

So, the infrastructure established in the Constitution gradually eroded an collapsed into the dung heap of federal hierarchy. It Sounds like what this man is seeing is breakup of the old system, perhaps it's actually restoration.

text:
**Where to post requests.** 
Wherever people actually are. A federal or multistate clearinghouse with an open API, mirrored to whatever public platform the moment favors, so a county in the Delta can put out a call and a church van from Georgia and a union local from Ohio can both see it the same hour.

---

## Section 8 — The Public Is Watching, and That Is the Point

Sunlight is not a nice extra here. It is the enforcement mechanism, and it is cheaper than an inspector general.

**Milestones.** Every project reports at 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100 percent completion. Each report carries timestamped photographs from fixed public vantage points, hours logged by trade, materials received with receipts attached, cost to date against estimate, and a plain-English note on anything that went sideways.

**Comment.** A public comment window opens at every milestone, and the project manager answers on the record. Not a form. An answer.

**Closeout ledger.** Within thirty days of completion the jurisdiction publishes estimated versus actual on every line: labor value, credits issued, materials, administration, injuries, claims, change orders, and what was learned.

**Vantage.** Where it is safe, the site stays visible. People should be able to walk past on Tuesday and see what their neighbors did on Saturday. The visible progress is half the civic value of the whole thing.

**Privacy, held firm.** A volunteer may opt out of publication of their name and face and still receive full credit. Recognition is offered, never extracted. Photographs of children require guardian consent. The published data is about the work and the money, and it is never a registry of who participates in civic life.

---

## Section 9 — Honor Them Loudly

Do not underestimate this part. Gratitude is the cheapest input in the entire program and it may be the one that decides whether anybody shows up in year three.

Annual Civic Service Awards. A public honor roll for those who want their name on it. Medals, ceremonies, a handshake from somebody who was actually elected. Let the kids meet the people who rebuilt their park.

And then let it get competitive, because Americans cannot help themselves. Neighborhood against neighborhood. High school against high school. Firefighters against electricians against plumbers against the accountants, who will show up in matching shirts and take it far too seriously. Cities challenging the city down the road. Something halfway between a county fair and the Olympics, with a trophy nobody can eat and everybody wants.

Who rebuilt the most playgrounds. Who planted the most trees. Which neighborhood hauled off the most trash. Which engineering team cracked the hardest accessibility problem. Which senior class logged the most hours.

But the honor tracks the work and nothing else. Never *you supported the correct cause.* Always *you gave 186 verified hours rebuilding homes after the tornado.* That single distinction is the wall between a civic program and a patronage machine, so build it high.

And a host community that treats visiting volunteers well will get them back. Feed them. Put their names on the sign if they want it there. Let the mayor show up with coffee at seven in the morning instead of a camera at noon.

text: All due respect, and I mean it, we disagree. The Pirate 🏴‍☠️ Empire. Read the sequence, then tell me what to call it. In January the United States seized Venezuela’s president in a night raid on Caracas and flew him and his wife to a courtroom in Manhattan, where they go on trial next year. His vice-president became interim president. That same month Caracas passed a hydrocarbons law gutting PDVSA and letting private firms work the wells directly. Sanctions came off. And on Friday night that same interim president signed, handing Washington 55 per cent of a venture holding hundred-year concessions over 63bn barrels of proven reserves. Eight months from the raid to the signature, and the counterparty holds office because Washington removed the last one. Ricardo Hausmann, once Venezuela’s planning minister, now at Harvard, says that government has no legitimacy to strike an unconstitutional deal. Francisco Rodríguez calls it predatory, says it contravenes the constitution, and adds the four words that settle it, at gunpoint. Both are economists. Neither is a politician. And this is why it will not last. The first constitutional government Venezuela produces will repudiate it, and the brief writes itself. Signed under duress. Signed by an administration the buyer installed. Signed over resources the constitution reserves to the nation. A hundred-year asset resting on a defective title from the first day. The D’Arcy concession in Persia was written to run sixty years. It was nationalised at fifty and the coup came two years after that, and everyone in Latin America knows how that story ends. But notice what separates this from the old imperialism. Trump announced it on Truth Social in capital letters and promised it would lower petrol prices for Americans. Not strategy, not security, not even the pretence of development. A South American country’s oil, sold to voters as relief at the pump ten weeks before an election. And it is a template, by his own admission. Threatening to seize Kharg Island last week, he said the United States would assume total control of Iran’s oil and gas markets, much like we have with Venezuela, which is working out brilliantly. Venezuela was the pilot. This is what a government looks like once the line between the state and the family running it has dissolved. At home, a Justice Department shielding the president’s tax records, a fund of 1.8bn to pay allies with public money, his face pressed onto a proposed banknote, and two sons holding both bitcoin and a dollar stablecoin so that no currency outcome can hurt them. Abroad, the same operation with a flag over it. The looting simply found a bigger jurisdiction. Moscow does this openly now. Washington has decided to compete. Every government in this hemisphere sitting on lithium, copper or crude watched the whole sequence, from the raid to the signature to the price of gasoline in Ohio, and they will go looking for a counterweight. There is only one on offer. The era of open imperialism was supposed to be over. What ended was the shame.

text:
The Woman Who Started Over With Nothing

In the summer of 1976, Tina Turner reached a breaking point.

For years, the world had known her as one half of one of music’s biggest acts. Behind the spotlight, however, her life had become a nightmare.

One night, she made a decision that would change everything.

With only 36 cents and a gasoline card, Tina escaped.

She ran through the darkness along a Texas highway, eventually reaching a Ramada Inn. Her face bore the visible aftermath of violence. The hotel manager recognized her, offered her shelter, and arranged security outside her room.

For several days, Tina disappeared from public view.

She had escaped the marriage.

But escaping her old life would be much harder.

When the divorce was settled, Tina did something few expected. She did not fight to keep the money, the property, or the music business rights connected to her former partnership.

Instead, she made one request that would prove far more valuable than anything else:

She wanted the name Tina Turner.

She left with serious debts and very little else.

And she was nearly 40.

To many people in the music industry, her story was already over. Her biggest success seemed to belong to the past.

Tina disagreed.

She accepted whatever performances she could find. Hotel rooms. Small venues. Fairs. Corporate functions.

There was no glamorous comeback waiting for her.

She rebuilt it one audience at a time.

Then, in 1984, everything changed.

At 44, Tina Turner released Private Dancer.

The album became an international phenomenon. “What’s Love Got to Do with It” brought her to the top of the charts, while Grammy Awards confirmed what she had fought to prove:

She was not a former star trying to survive.

She was a star in her own right.

What followed became one of the greatest second acts in music history. Tina Turner went on to become a global icon, selling more than 100 million records over her career.

Her personal life eventually changed too. She found lasting happiness with Erwin Bach, with whom she built a quieter life in Switzerland.

When Tina Turner died at 83, she left behind unforgettable songs and a legacy far greater than commercial success.

Her life became a reminder that a beginning can come after devastation.

You can lose your home.

You can lose your money.

You can lose years.

You can lose everything people think defines you.

And still have enough left to rebuild.

Sometimes, all you need is the one thing no one else can take from you:

the courage to begin again.

**Sec. 7. Caps.** *[Section 4.3 limits.]*

**Sec. 8. Interstate Reciprocity.** *[Section 7 guardrails, invitation-only, no conditions.]*

**Sec. 9. Audit and Sunset.** This Act expires five years from the effective date. It shall not be renewed except by affirmative recorded vote following publication of the report required herein.

---

## Section 14 — The Tensions Worth Keeping

Justice without liberty turns into authoritarianism.
Liberty without responsibility turns into neglect.
Compassion without restraint turns into dependency and graft.
Strength without mercy turns into brutality.

The constitutional job is holding all of them in tension at once. Establish justice, insure domestic tranquility, provide for the common defence, promote the general welfare, and through every bit of it, secure the blessings of liberty not only for ourselves but for the people coming after us who never got a vote on any of it.

Posterity is the part we skip. A government can make today comfortable by borrowing what tomorrow has to repay. It can build surveillance powers that look harmless under this administration and terrifying under the next one. It can let the bridges rust and call the savings a surplus. So every program, including this one, should have to answer a plain question:

> Are we handing our children more liberty and more opportunity than we received, or are we just sending them the bill?

Here is the hopeful part, and it deserves the last word in the body of this proposal. Most of what makes a place good to live in has never come from a statute. It came from people who showed up. A statute can only clear the brush and hold the light. The playground still gets fixed by somebody's daddy on a Saturday with a socket set, and that has always been true, and it is still true, and the arithmetic in Section 4 says we can afford to thank him for it.

A more perfect union is a living thing we build when we love our neighbors. And if a reasonable tax break gets a few Scrooges out there fixing playgrounds too, well, why not. 🪷

---

## Appendix A — A Note on Faith, Offered Voluntarily

*This appendix is the author's personal statement. It is deliberately not part of the proposal, and no provision above depends on it or advances it. That separation is the argument.*

A country does not become Christian because Congress hangs a cross somewhere. If Christians actually love God and treat their neighbors as they want to be treated, the influence shows up in what gets done. Mercy. Courage. Forgiveness. Service. Education. Protection of the weak. Hospitality. Self-restraint. Truth. Love toward enemies, which is the hard one and the whole test.

That last one matters most where our leaders abandon it fastest. Fear, war, and power are exactly the conditions under which the Golden Rule gets suspended, and the blowback is all around us in surveillance, in debt, in wars with no end, in support for things a great many of us regard as atrocities. Sometimes force really is necessary. Lethal is not the same as cruel. Defense does not require dishonor, betrayal, torture, or hatred.

Somebody else is free to call every one of those virtues humanism, Judaism, Islam, secular ethics, plain philosophy, or just being a decent neighbor. The Constitution protects that disagreement, and I want it protected.

A Christian nation produced by Christian conduct is a different creature from Christianity installed by state power. The first can change a culture from the inside. The second corrupts both the faith and the government, and it usually corrupts the faith first.

That is how the meek inherit the earth, and how the Kingdom starts showing up here. 🪷

The Cauvery delta holds three exceptional seven-temple heritage circuits:

• Thiruvaiyaru Saptha Sthanam — Thiruvaiyaru, Thillaisthanam, Thirupazhanam, Thiruppoonthuruthi, Kandiyur, Thiruvedikudi and Thiruchotruthurai

• Saptha Mangai Sthalams around Ayyampettai — seven Shiva temples associated with the Sapta Matrikas

• Saptha Vidanga Sthalams — Tiruvarur, Tirunallar, Nagapattinam, Tirukkuvalai, Vedaranyam, Tiruvaimur and Tirukkaravasal, each associated with a distinctive form of Tyagaraja’s sacred dance

Together, these circuits unite inscriptions, Chola art, river landscapes, ritual traditions and living community worship. They offer strong potential for carefully planned heritage journeys.

Clear approach-road signs, circuit maps, multilingual information boards, QR-linked histories, coordinated temple timings, basic amenities and trained local guides can improve access and support local communities.

At the same time, these remain sacred spaces rather than mass-tourism destinations. 

Visitor planning should respect worship, processions, temple timings, architectural sensitivity and the quiet character of the surrounding villages. 

Commercial clutter, intrusive infrastructure and unmanaged crowds should give way to small-scale, responsible and community-led tourism.

At the same time many of these temples needs our continuous patronage 

Tamil Nadu and #incredibleIndia can present these temples as connected heritage journeys while preserving the spirituality that gives them meaning.

text:
The Honourable Minister of Information and National Orientation, @HMMohammedIdris’s speech at the celebration of Taraba State at 35, in Jalingo, this week #TarabaAt35

I am delighted to be in Taraba State today, and I bring warm greetings from His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, and the Federal Executive Council.

It is a great honour to join the government and people of Taraba in celebrating 35 years of statehood and, importantly, in witnessing the unveiling of a blueprint that looks beyond the achievements of the past to the possibilities of the future.

Thirty-five years is a significant milestone. Since its creation on 27 August 1991, Taraba has developed into a state distinguished by its cultural diversity, agricultural potential, natural resources and remarkable landscapes.

It is not by accident that Taraba's slogan is “Nature's Gift to the Nation.” It reflects the beauty and fertility of the State's terrain and landscape, and the warmth and welcoming nature of its people. It is home to Chappal Waddi, Nigeria's highest mountain, the Gashaka-Gumti National Park and the iconic Mambilla Plateau. 

It is home to nourishing rivers, including the one from which it gets its name. And in its ethnic diversity, Taraba represents a remarkable microcosm of Nigeria, with numerous communities and cultures living together.

Taraba is also one of Nigeria's important agricultural frontiers. Its fertile lowlands support the cultivation of crops such as yam, rice, cassava, millet and maize, while the highlands offer opportunities in crops such as tea and coffee, alongside significant livestock production. Its rivers and water resources also give the state enormous potential for hydropower and other forms of energy development.

What this means is that Taraba's greatest asset is not simply what is beneath the ground or the beauty of its landscape. It is the economic value that can be created from these resources, through agriculture and agro-processing, livestock, energy, tourism, manufacturing and other productive activities.

However, an anniversary is not only about looking back. It is also about asking: What kind of future are we building? That is what makes today's unveiling of the Taraba Regional Development Master Plan so significant.

Development requires vision, planning and consistency. A master plan provides a framework for coordinated growth, responsible investment, infrastructure development and better use of public resources. I commend Governor Agbu Kefas and the Taraba State Government for embracing this long-term approach.

I also acknowledge the progress being made by the Taraba State Government across areas such as education, healthcare, infrastructure, economic development, security and social cohesion. 

The decision to make primary and secondary education free and compulsory is particularly important, given the central role of education in building the human capital that Taraba will require for its next phase of development. 

The State Government has also continued to support students by meeting examination costs, including more than ₦1.8 billion provided in 2026 for NECO, BECE and NABTEB registration for public-school students.

The recent financing secured by Taraba from the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development is another significant development. In June this year, EBID and the Taraba State Government signed financing agreements totalling about $268 million for an integrated industrial park, 10,000 hectares of irrigated rice production and processing, and a 50-megawatt solar power plant in Jalingo. These are precisely the kinds of investments that can connect Taraba's natural advantages to jobs, production, value addition and economic growth.

The Federal Government under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu shares this commitment to deliberate and inclusive development. Indeed, Taraba is already benefiting from this vision.

text:
Most market participants view index concentration as a valuation argument. It is not. It is a volatility and liquidity plumbing dynamic. ​Two quantitative shops analyzed S&P 500 concentration and reached opposite conclusions:

1.) ​D. E. Shaw showed the top ten names account for 39.1% of index cap and 57.4% of index volatility. Risk contribution is 1.5 times their weight.

2.) ​Elm Wealth showed the market was just as concentrated in the 1930s and 1950s. The expected return penalty for cap weighting is roughly 0.08%, and trying to time concentration lagged buy-and-hold.

​Both are right because they measure different variables. Shaw measures risk contribution; Elm measures expected return.

​Our risk decomposition on current holdings:

​• Nvidia: 8.29% weight vs. 16.01% volatility contribution
• Alphabet: 5.40% weight vs. 7.29% volatility contribution
• Broadcom: 2.64% weight vs. 5.72% volatility contribution
• Micron: 1.58% weight vs. 5.35% volatility contribution
• Apple: 6.94% weight vs. 5.05% volatility contribution
• JPMorgan: 1.42% weight vs. 1.11% volatility contribution

​Waiting for mean reversion is a flawed strategy. For top ten weight to revert to its pre-2020 baseline while mega-caps stay flat, the other 490 stocks must rally over 160%.

​Concentration does not cost you expected return, but it concentrates your drawdown risk into a handful of balance sheets. ​In macro allocation, you never time an arbitrary multiple. You budget your volatility, evaluate asymmetry, and protect capital first.

​Sources: D. E. Shaw Group, Elm Wealth, State Street, Yahoo Finance. Analysis: Momentum Wealth Management
