This is My Final Review of Nolan's Odyssey

I'm glad to learn that Mr. Musk intends to make an "Odyssey" movie of his own. I have a Master of Arts degree in History. I possess expertise in ancient Greek history and culture. Here follows the third of three postings I intend to make here at X in which I criticize Nolan's version of the "Odyssey."

Okay. I’ve seen it. That means I have now earned the right to criticize it. And so I will. It’s two hours and fifty-two minutes too long. It’s a bust and no amount of seventy-millimeter film can save it. It’s not Homer. It’s a desecration of Homer. It grossly misrepresents Homer where fidelity to Homer is a moral imperative.
The look and feel of the movie are simply all wrong. The knowledgeable viewer wants to be swept up in Homer’s tale, but the blatant errors are so obvious that the necessary suspension of disbelief is impossible. Every error jerks the viewer out of the story and into wondering what the hell Nolan was thinking.
For example, the helmets and armor are ludicrously bad, groaningly untrue to what the Greeks and Trojans wore. They look like they are made of rubber, not bronze. Agamemnon’s helmet is particularly bad. It looks like Batman’s cowl. Perhaps Nolan was subconsciously channeling his previous commercial successes with his Batman movies. And the fearsome giants who destroy some of Odysseus’s ships are shown wearing comical spaceman suit-like armor which would come as a surprise to Homer.
The Trojan horse is implausibly portrayed as being a finely worked statue and reared up on its hind legs. The Trojan horse, as depicted in the 2004 movie "Troy," looked authentically crude and improvised.  Furthermore, Troy didn’t look like Morocco.
Miscastings abound. Our received vision of Circe is that she was a dangerous young beauty, not the tired, middle-aged figure Nolan gives us. Zendaya is wholly inadequate as Athena. Where is her statuesque presence? Where is her helmet? Where is her owl? Where is the aegis figure on the front of her garment? Where are her famously piercing gray eyes?
Nolan’s movie offers a catalog of missed opportunities. Where is Odysseus’s mischievous banter with the Cyclops? Where is the “test of the bed” scene which forms the emotionally searing climax of Odysseus’s homecoming?
No, Homer’s Odysseus did not suffer from PTSD and guilt trips as Nolan would have us believe. Reading Homer, Virgil, and Quintus of Smyrna, one gets the impression that Odysseus was actually pretty pleased with himself for devising the strategy that won the Trojan War and for so masterfully using his wits to make it home in spite of all.
Worst of all, the movie panders to “woke” sensibilities at the expense of integrity in art. As we all know, Hollywood has declared its absurd and fundamentally evil policy that a film must meet quotas of representing minorities in the cast if said film hopes to be considered for an Oscar. Nolan, in an act of artistic cowardice, has bent the knee to this policy. He has reduced himself to being an artistic whore. As a result, we are forced to watch a puny, five-foot-nothing former woman/trans man attempt to impersonate an ancient Greek warrior. Yeah, right. The sight and sound of a modern-day, smack-talking, Black American rapper impersonating a Bronze Age Greek bard is obscene. Nolan forces us to watch and listen as a couple of Black guys identify themselves, with straight faces, as “we’re just Greeks from Ithaca.” And having a sub-Saharan Black woman try to inhabit the role of the most beautiful woman in the Greek world is the last word in artistic depravity. There were no Black people in Bronze Age Greece. The deep tragedy in all this is that American audiences are so ignorant of their own histories that this movie will wrongfully convince them that some ancient Greeks were Black! Now let’s see what happens if Hollywood makes a biopic about Martin Luther King with a White actor in the lead role. . . .
In sum, Nolan’s Odyssey is an act of cultural genocide. It is one more sign of the ever-accelerating erasure of an entire race’s heritage. It’s an outrage. I regret that I contributed the price of my ticket toward the success of this outrage.

text:
The prosecution offered plea agreements.

My mother accepted first.

She agreed to testify against the others in exchange for a reduced sentence.

That decision ended whatever remained of my parents’ marriage.

My father called her a traitor in open court.

I almost laughed at the absurdity.

They had left a child to die, yet they believed betrayal was something only other people could commit.

My mother testified for two days.

She described the planning meetings at Melissa’s house. She admitted writing the note. She admitted helping remove water, food, blankets, and first-aid supplies.

“Did you know Daniel’s phone would not have service?” the prosecutor asked.

“Yes.”

“Did you know the temperature could fall below freezing?”

“Yes.”

“Did you know your nine-year-old grandson was hiking with him?”

“Yes.”

“Why didn’t you stop the plan?”

My mother looked toward the jury.

“I thought Daniel would manage.”

The prosecutor lifted a photograph of Noah being carried into the helicopter.

“This is what managing looked like.”

My mother lowered her eyes.

My father’s attorney argued that the family had expected us to follow the road to safety. But the prosecution presented the stolen road signs and Troy’s map showing the most confusing intersections.

Melissa’s attorney claimed she was afraid of her husband.

Then prosecutors displayed her messages.

Take Daniel’s car keys before he leaves for the hike.

Make sure the kid doesn’t have his tablet.

Don’t leave even one bottle of water.

Her fear had not prevented her from being thorough.

Troy’s defense focused on the financial motive. His attorneys argued that pressuring me to invest was not proof that he intended us to die.

Then the prosecutor played a recording recovered from my father’s laptop.

The four of them had held a video call one week before the trip.

Troy’s voice filled the courtroom.

“If Daniel has to spend one cold night out there, he’ll understand that family support is not automatic.”

Melissa laughed.

My father said, “Two nights might be better.”

My mother asked, “What about Noah?”

There was a pause.

Then Troy answered.

“The boy is Daniel’s weakness. He’ll agree faster if Noah is uncomfortable.”

No one objected.

No one said stop.

The courtroom remained completely silent after the recording ended.

When it was my turn to testify, I walked past my family without looking at them.

I described returning to the empty clearing.

I described the note.

I described Noah asking whether we were going to die.

I described the cold, the hunger, his fever, the locked gate, and the helicopter.

The prosecutor handed me the original note.

“Do you recognize this?”

“Yes.”

“How did it make you feel?”

I looked at the paper inside the evidence sleeve.

“At first, abandoned.”

I turned toward the defendants.

“Now it reminds me that my son and I survived people who wanted us to feel helpless.”

My father stared at the table.

Melissa cried.

Troy watched me with the same flat expression he had worn throughout the trial.

Noah was not required to testify in the courtroom. Instead, the judge allowed a recorded interview conducted by a trained child specialist……

text:
Tulsa County District Attorney Seeks Removal of Judge Sharon Holmes From Six Criminal Cases

Tulsa County District Attorney Steve Kunzweiler’s office wants Judge Sharon Holmes removed from six criminal cases.

The reasons are not minor.

Prosecutors say Holmes held private conversations with criminal defendants and their supporters without disclosing what was discussed. They say she also spoke privately with a jury and refused to tell either side what was said.

They further allege she discussed the possibility of a defendant doing construction work at her home and accepted another defendant’s offer to bring her lunch.

Holmes declined to recuse herself. Another Tulsa County judge, David Guten, denied the DA’s request, ruling there was not sufficient legal reason to remove her.

This is not the first time the DA’s office has tried to get Holmes off cases. One previous request succeeded. Another case ended in a mistrial after similar concerns were raised.

Holmes has pushed back, saying in court documents that Kunzweiler has “always had an issue” with her and is focused on her for reasons she calls unwarranted.

The DA’s office says its priority is justice for victims and that when it sees conduct that could undermine a fair outcome, it has an obligation to act.

Private conversations with defendants. Private talks with a jury. Personal favors.

These are the kinds of allegations that go straight to public trust in the courtroom.

Whether the current recusal requests succeed or not, the pattern is now on the record.

text:
Why can large language models seemingly “pull themselves up by their own bootstraps” and continue improving?

Beyond higher-quality expert data and better training infrastructure with fewer bugs, one important reason is reinforcement learning during post-training.

In 2025, UCLA mathematics professor Ernest K. Ryu @ErnestRyu who also works as a researcher at OpenAI—offered a course titled Reinforcement Learning for LLMs. The lecture videos and notes are freely available on his website. I have worked through roughly half of the course so far.

While the ideas are still fresh in my mind, I wrote a short blog post explaining policy updates in the simplest way I could. My main takeaway is that visualizing policy updates as a decision tree provides a useful framework for understanding reinforcement learning in LLMs. Once this intuition is in place, concepts such as KL divergence and trust regions become much easier to understand.

text:
The US establishment is threatening to deliver a debilitating 100% tariff blow to the Indian economy if it buys Urals crude. This is neither the eccentricity of US President Donald Trump nor MAGA madness, but a sure-footed step by the brute bipartisan majority of the US Senate. This move is being pushed by a “mainstream, liberal, progressive and conventional” senator from Connecticut, Richard Blumenthal — as blue as any Democratic Party senator ever could be. He was a classmate of Bill and Hillary Clinton at Yale; Michelle and Barack campaigned for him; and he was friends with Biden’s late son. 
Granted, the process has only begun in the Senate, where there will be a detailed debate and possible amendments. After that, there will be a cloture vote if the debate rambles on, and then the final passage vote. From the Senate, the bill goes to the House of Representatives before being sent to the President for signature. The bill does not impose a 100% tariff right away but gives the tariff-happy president the power to impose tariffs of up to 100% against India and China.
This gives “the main culprits” a great opportunity to get together for another huddle along with Russia. In fact, it was Russia that helped the two Asian giants walk back from the Himalayan brink by offering a platform for peace at Kazan on October 23, 2024, on the sidelines of the BRICS summit. India presides over this year’s BRICS summit, expected to be held in Delhi on September 12 and 13. If Kazan helped thaw relations and Tianjin created the optics for a multipolar world, Delhi should draw up the sea map for a Russia-China-India eastern energy and trade corridor from Vladivostok to Shanghai to Chennai — a peaceful, strong, maritime route away from the piracy-ridden Western seas.
The US has been hostile to India ever since the latter refused to act as a proxy to contain China in the Himalayas. The deadly Pahalgam terror attack and India’s response, Operation Sindoor, made things worse, with the Western press praising Pakistan with war poetry over falling Rafale jets (now, expectedly, there has been little reporting on claims that Iranian attacks struck F-35s) and Trump hailing his favourite Field Marshal. Then there were tariff threats. That was the moment that led to the Tianjin huddle. It is time for another — one that should go beyond optics and be rooted in assurances of mutual respect, territorial integrity, non-aggression, non-interference and boundless trade.
A BRICS currency does not seem ready to become a reality, considering how cautious India is in taking every step in the Western geopolitical minefield. The colonial redux could not have been more stark. The legislature of a nation lying 13,000 km away wants to control Indian trade and, by extension, global oil flows. And India, the world’s third-largest oil importer, is being stopped from accessing these two sources to ensure superprofits for the Anglo-American oil companies.
This US diktat offers India and China a rare opportunity to trade in their own currencies — a $150 billion rupee-yuan trade would strengthen Asian currencies without introducing a new BRICS one. The 'Lines' in the Video Explained in Candace's video

The distinct lines visible in the video Candace Owens shared are scanlines or "moire patterns." This physical distortion occurs exclusively when someone uses a smartphone or external camera to record a digital playback monitor, such as a laptop screen or a television.

The presence of these lines confirms the exact setting where the clip was captured:

The Context: Because the Fourth District Court in Utah has heavily restricted the raw digital files from being leaked to the general public, independent media figures and attendees have had to physically record the courtroom projection screens during the July 2026 preliminary hearings.

The Source: The "lines" are a product of recording a courtroom presentation monitor with a second device, rather than downloading the unedited source video file straight from Utah Valley University's security network.

Why the Footage Looks So 'Grainy'

Standard CCTV Limitations: The video comes from fixed, outdoor campus security cameras positioned at a significant distance from the Losee Center roof. Standard security cameras are optimized for wide-area coverage rather than high-definition zooming, resulting in highly pixelated or "grainy" figures when zoomed in on a specific person.

The Legal Interlock: Because the video quality itself doesn't offer a crystal-clear look at the weapon, the legal case doesn't rely on the video alone. Instead, prosecutors are connecting the grainy footage to physical evidence recovered on the ground—specifically, the Mauser .30-06 bolt-action rifle found hidden in the nearby woods wrapped in a towel that carried Tyler Robinson's DNA.

The visual artifacts and low resolution are precisely why the trial evidence has become a Rorschach test online: skeptics look at the grain and see an impossible logistical narrative, while forensic investigators treat the video as just a timeline anchor for the matching DNA and text confessions.

text:
In April 1861 Robert E. Lee had the hardest choice of his life, and he made it pacing the floor of his house at Arlington all night long.

He had just been offered command of the entire Union army. Thirty two years in that uniform. Winfield Scott, his old mentor, wanted him to lead. Lincoln's people wanted him to lead. Lee did not even believe in secession. He called it revolution and said if he owned every slave in the South he would give them all up to save the Union.

But he was a Virginian. His family had been Virginian for generations. And when Virginia voted to leave, he could not bring himself to draw his sword against his own home, his own neighbors, his own children.

So he sat up all night in the room above the Potomac, walking back and forth, and by morning he had written out his resignation. He gave up the biggest command in the country to fight for a cause he had doubts about, purely because of where he was born. He wrote to his sister that he could not raise his hand against his relatives, his children, his home, even as he could not see the necessity of breaking up the country.

One man, one night, two loyalties that could not both survive. He chose the ground under his feet over the flag he had served his whole life, and it decided the shape of the war.

text:
How Long Will I Grieve?
by Michael Whelan 

People ask me that question a lot.

"Michael... how long do you think this grief will last?"

These days I usually smile, though it's the kind of smile that carries more sadness than comfort.

Then I quietly answer,
"How long do you think Rebecca will be dead?"

Unfortunately...
...about that long.

Not because grief never changes.

It does.

But because love doesn't end simply because breathing does.
We've been taught to believe grief is something to conquer, something to graduate from, something with an expiration date. As though one morning we'll wake up, brush our teeth, pour our coffee, and discover we've finally "moved on."

Love doesn't work that way.

Neither does grief.

Grief is simply love searching for someone who is no longer there.

The greatest misunderstanding about grief is that people think we need to be fixed.

We don't.

We need to be witnessed.

Held tightly.

There is an enormous difference.

Don't hand me a silver lining while my world is still covered in ashes.

Don't tell me she's in a better place when the place I wanted her was sitting beside me on the couch.

Don't rush me toward tomorrow because today makes you uncomfortable.

Just sit beside me.

Listen.

Let me tell the same story for the hundredth time if that's what my heart needs. 

Every time I speak her name, I'm not refusing to heal. I'm refusing to let fifty-six years of extraordinary love disappear into silence.

That isn't dwelling.

That's remembering.

That's honoring.

That's love.

People often ask when grief gets easier.
I don't know that it becomes easier.
I think we become stronger. We learn to carry grief easier-in time. 

The waves still come.

Some days they're gentle enough to let me breathe.
Other days they rise without warning—a song in the grocery store, her favorite coffee mug, an empty side of the bed—and suddenly I'm drowning all over again.

The ocean hasn't changed.

I've simply learned that I can survive another wave.

There is no timetable for missing the love of your life.

No calendar notification that reads,

Congratulations... today you are finished grieving.

Who decided twelve months was enough to mourn a lifetime?
The calendar keeps turning.

The heart doesn't.

I've learned something else during these past months.

The opposite of grief isn't happiness.

The opposite of grief is being unseen.

When someone truly witnesses your pain—without trying to solve it, compare it, minimize it, or outrun it—they offer one of the greatest gifts another human being can receive.

They quietly say,
"I see how much you loved."
And somehow...
that makes carrying the unbearable just a little more bearable.

So if you know someone who is grieving, don't worry about finding the perfect words.

There aren't any.

Your presence will always speak louder than your advice.

Sit beside them.

Hold their hand.

Say their loved one's name.

Let them cry.

Let them laugh when an old memory sneaks through the tears.

Bear witness.

Because grief is not a disease to cure.

It is the final, sacred act of loving someone who changed your life forever.
And as long as love remains...
so will grief.

Not as an enemy.

But as the quiet echo of a beautiful life that mattered.

The difference between earning $0 and reaching your first $100,000 in revenue is often resilience, the right connection at the right time, smart marketing, a spike in traffic, and a bit of luck.

No one will pay for your product if they cannot see it. Gaining visibility requires sacrifice, consistency, strategic marketing, and sometimes luck.

I keep emphasizing luck because I have experienced this firsthand during my last 5 years of focusing fully on entrepreneurship. Luck is difficult to come by. You may be extremely good at what you do and still struggle to get the right opportunity, connection, or exposure.

Someone who is not as experienced as you, or who started after you, may become more successful simply because they approached things differently, marketed themselves better, or made smarter decisions at the right time.

Reaching your first $100,000 in revenue as a bootstrapped solo entrepreneur is incredibly difficult.

Now that AI is part of the equation, many more entrepreneurs, builders, and products will emerge. The question you need to ask yourself is:

How can I use this #AI era to improve myself, build better products, and stand out?

Remember, millions of people are thinking about the same opportunities you are thinking about. This means the competition will become more intense than anything you have faced before.

However, not everyone is built for the journey.

Some people will give up after a few months when they do not see results. A smaller group will continue building, learning, experimenting, and trying different approaches until something finally works.

Do not feel discouraged when things are not working out yet.

Connect with people.

Put yourself out there.

Keep building.

Market yourself and your products.

Never stop learning, improving, and showing up.

One day, you may wake up to an unexpected message, a life-changing offer, a sudden spike in product #traffic , or hundreds of new subscriptions.

But none of these things will happen if you do not put in the work, remain visible, and stay consistent.

text:
After Negeri Sembilan: PH Must Build a Narrative and Walk the Talk
By Rajiv Rishyakaran, ADUN for Bukit Gasing

Yesterday’s election results in Negeri Sembilan are an unmistakable wake-up call. Coming on the heels of earlier setbacks in Sabah and Johor, the message from the electorate is loud and clear: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is losing ground because we are losing the battle of narratives.

Look at our opponents. Both Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) operate on a simple, crystal-clear—albeit terrible and deeply divisive—narrative: Malay unity. It is crude political arithmetic, but voters easily understand it.

What is Pakatan Harapan’s narrative in response? Right now, we have none. We offer voters no compelling reason to choose us beyond merely existing in office.

For DAP, holding roughly 20% of parliamentary seats means we are a vital partner in government, but not the sole decision-maker. We must evolve into a mature party of governance—without diluting our soul. Crucially, we must define a clear purpose of existence. Why should ordinary Malaysians want us in government beyond a lazy “we are better than them” mantra? 

We must do this while holding unyieldingly to non-negotiables: zero tolerance for corruption and total administrative transparency. It also means being transparent about a "Malaysian Malaysia"—upholding the Federal Constitution while being entirely upfront and honest about the socio-economic and racial formula we offer.

Beyond identity politics, we must anchor our purpose in a bold, 20-year social democratic vision. We should lead the fight on:
1.Fixing our collapsing public healthcare system,
2.Tackling low wages and crippling retirement gaps,
3.Accelerating the clean energy transition, and
4.Modernizing education for a competitive future.

A narrative, however, is useless if it remains trapped in press releases. It is extremely urgent and critical that Pakatan Harapan defines its core purpose and starts walking the talk immediately in the state and federal governments we still hold. We must demonstrate the tangible, real-world value of progressive and competent governance right now.

If we fail to offer voters a clear narrative and prove that we can deliver on it before the next General Election, our opponents’ divisive message will continue to win by default.

text:
One of the strangest things about social media is the existence of people who follow someone they can’t stand. They wake up, open various apps, and voluntarily spend part of their day consuming the thoughts of a person they claim to despise. They might tell themselves they’re watching because they’re exposing someone, waiting for a mistake, or proving themselves right. But your attention is the most valuable thing you possess. Wherever you direct it, you give your life force or chi away. If someone occupies your mind every day, they’ve become part of your life, whether you intended it or not.

I don’t understand it. Life is too short to build your days around resentment and hatred. If someone has nothing to offer you, unfollow them and move on. Fill your attention with people who make you wiser, kinder, stronger, or more present. Your mind becomes whatever you feed it. Hatred doesn’t punish the person you’re watching, but it does gradually reshape the one doing the watching.

text:
LETTERS FROM STOCKHOLM: OBASANJO, THE GRAVE IS NOT A WITNESS BOX — AND NEITHER IS YOUR EGO

By Kio Amachree

Twenty years after the Nigerian Senate buried the third term agenda, Olusegun Obasanjo is still fighting the war he lost in 2006. This past week alone, at a fireside conversation in Lagos, he declared that choosing Atiku Abubakar as his running mate in 1999 was the biggest mistake of his presidency. Days earlier he resurrected an allegation that Atiku bribed the late Speaker Ghali Na'Abba to impeach him — an accusation against a dead man who cannot rise to answer it. Atiku's reply was titled with surgical precision: the grave is not a witness box. Neither, I would add, is a Lagos fireside chat, a presidential library podium, or any of the endless platforms from which this man conducts his one-man tribunal against everyone who ever told him no.

Let us remember what actually happened in 2006. Obasanjo's people moved a constitutional amendment to hand him a third term. Legislators later spoke openly of inducements offered to grease its passage. The Senate, to its eternal credit, killed it on the floor in May 2006, live on television, and the man most responsible for stiffening the opposition was his own vice president. That is Atiku's unforgivable sin. Not corruption. Not incompetence. He said no to a man who has never once heard the word without plotting revenge. Every attack since — the recycled allegations, the rewritten history, the crocodile regrets — flows from that single wound to a bottomless ego. And the timing now is transparent: 2027 is taking shape, Atiku carries the ADC flag, and Baba is clearing the runway for his preferred kinsman. This is not elder statesmanship. It is kingmaking by character assassination.

Let us also be honest about who is lecturing Nigeria on virtue. This is the president on whose watch soldiers razed Odi in Bayelsa in November 1999 and Zaki-Biam in Benue in 2001 — entire communities put to the torch, women and old men among the dead, collective punishment as state policy. He has never truly answered for either. This is the president who, while still in office, acquired shares in Transcorp, a conglomerate bidding for state assets his own government was privatising, a conflict of interest so brazen it would end a career in any serious democracy. This is the man who raised billions for his presidential library while still holding the levers of power, with businessmen and governors falling over themselves to donate to the man who could still bless or break them. Ill-gotten gains parked behind so-called billionaire fronts, favours laundered through philanthropy — and today he wags his finger at the nation like a village headmaster.

My family remembers an older version of this same man. My father, Chief Godfrey Kio Jaja Amachree QC — Nigeria's first Solicitor-General, first African Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations — laboured for reconciliation and the end of the civil war. For that service he was awarded an oil prospecting license in 1969, the first private Nigerian holder of such a bloc. When he declined to use his standing with the American oil companies to run errands for Obasanjo's benefit, that license became a target and the harassment became full time. Serve me or be destroyed: that has always been the Obasanjo method, tribal vindictiveness dressed in agbada and called governance. It is no different in kind from what we condemn in Tinubu today, and the elders of my father's generation could tell you exactly where certain self-declared war heroes were found when soldiers came looking during the coup years — and it was not at the front. My father himself once had to put Obasanjo firmly in his place aboard a Caledonian Airways flight, when a then down-and-out former head of state insisted on planting himself in first class with a second class ticket. The entitlement never left him. It simply acquired a library.

Even the military legend is largely self-published. Read the accounts of officers who served in the 3rd Marine Commando: the hard, bloody grinding of that campaign was done under others, and Obasanjo arrived in time to accept the surrender in January 1970 and then spent the next five decades writing himself into the centre of the story. "My Command" indeed — the most accurate title he ever chose, since "my" is the only pronoun he has ever fully mastered. This is the George Washington of Nigeria? Washington surrendered power once and went home to Mount Vernon in silence. Cincinnatus returned to his plough. Obasanjo tore up his party card for the cameras, writes open letters titled "Before It Is Too Late" as though he were not himself the author of much of the lateness, and cannot surrender a microphone even at eighty-nine.

And the moral sermons? This is a man whose own household has answered him. His son's sworn divorce filings contained family allegations so disgraceful I will not repeat them in print — allegations he denied, but which the whole country read, and which sit rather awkwardly beneath the halo he polishes daily. A man whose own blood petitions the courts against him should approach the pulpit with humility, not a megaphone.

Nigeria's 2027 conversation belongs to the living and the young. It should be about the grid that still collapses, the naira that still bleeds, the bandits who still tax our highways, and the millions of brilliant young Nigerians planning their escape from their own country. It should not be held hostage by the recycled grudges of a serial score-settler auditioning, one last time, as kingmaker. Atiku is right that the objective is to confer advantage on a preferred candidate. Nigerians are too discerning for it. We can smell a stale vendetta from Stockholm.

So let it be said plainly. Sit down, Baba. Quietly. Write your memoirs — you have had plenty of practice inventing them. Tend the farm at Ota. Let Nigeria breathe. This country needs a younger, modern leader with no tribal baggage, no military mythology, no billionaire fronts, and no appetite whatsoever for the treasury. No more recycled generals. No more self-anointed fathers of the nation. No more Washington stooges.

A fresh start — or nothing.

Kio Amachree writes from Stockholm. He is Founder and President of Worldview International.

text:
Trump tariffs target India again

By Prabhu Chawla 

India, the more cooperative partner, has been the more frequently punished. Keeping in view the importance of strategic partnership, India has been making significant concessions.

In the long arc of democratic history, the spectacle of the world’s richest democracy systematically hounding the world’s largest and fastest-growing democracy should provoke more than routine diplomatic furore. It should force a reckoning with what power has become when it confuses leverage with leadership. Donald Trump has turned the instruments of diplomacy into tools of coercion and intimidation. That coercion has fixated with particular intensity on India. Trade and commerce have been weaponised. Trump has converted them from a means of building consensus into a blunt instrument for dictating the terms of trade and imposing asymmetrical pressure on any partner that fails to yield at once.

The result is not statecraft, but a sustained campaign of economic destabilisation that undermines the very norms of reciprocity upon which stable international relations are built. The latest and most provocative action arrived last week, hours after the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham at Washington National Cathedral, where Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Benjamin Netanyahu stood among the mourners, when the US Senate voted 86-12 to advance the Graham’s legislation, Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.

The legislation authorises secondary tariffs of up to 100 percent on countries that continue to purchase Russian oil and gas. An earlier draft had explicitly named India, China, Slovakia, Hungary and Azerbaijan as targets. Trump’s fear and favour were clearly reflected in the provisions of the Act. It carefully exempted 15 European nations still importing Russian gas on the grounds that their volumes represented a smaller and declining share of demand.

India buys oil, but then, Europe buys gas. Only one category was judged suitable for maximum pressure. That bipartisan statute—advanced after a colleague’s funeral with more than 60 co-sponsors from both parties—is far harder to reverse than any presidential order. It represents the institutionalization of coercive diplomacy, transforming a temporary executive preference into enduring legislative mandate.

This vote is the culmination of a campaign that has already altered the duty on Indian goods five times in 15 months. Each one of the penal changes were calibrated to extract further concessions rather than to establish a durable framework. In April 2025, Washington threatened a 26 percent tariff. By August, the rate stood at 50 percent, the additional 25 points imposed solely because India continued to purchase Russian crude. Earlier this year, Trump and Modi announced an interim understanding that lowered the rate to 18 percent in return for $500 billion in promised Indian purchases of American energy, technology and other goods.

Eighteen days later, the US Supreme Court, in a 6-3 opinion authored by Chief Justice John Roberts, ruled that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act never authorised those tariffs, voiding more than $160 billion already collected and rendering the India understanding moot. Trump absorbed the judicial setback and immediately imposed a flat 10 percent surcharge under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974.

When that temporary authority expired on July 24, Section 301 duties of 10 percent took effect the same night, justified by findings on forced-labour enforcement. Five successive rates, one country, 15 months—an unbroken sequence of recalibration conveying a sordid saga of undiplomatic conduct. It’s for the first time in America’s 250-year-old history that its Head of State has acquired the image of a bully with scant regards for conviction and consistency.

China, which imports comparable volumes of Russian oil, has faced no such revolving door of punishment and has been offered something closer to a negotiated truce. India, the more cooperative partner, has been the more frequently punished. Keeping in view the importance of strategic partnership, India has been making significant concessions. The US goods trade deficit with India stood at around $58 billion in 2025, 27 percent higher than the year before.

However, India’s own surplus with the US narrowed to $34.4 billion in 2025-26 from $40.9 billion the previous year. India reduced the share of its crude imports drawn from Russia, increased purchases of American energy and kept the negotiating channels open while Indian firms committed substantial new investment on American soil. More than a dozen rounds of high-level negotiations followed by visits of senior officials to both Washington and New Delhi have taken place. But they have been turned into either photo albums, TV bytes, or been dismissed by Trump as irrelevant for now.

None of these adjustments has produced a stable rate, a durable exemption, or even a settled legal basis for the duties currently applied. Cooperativeness has been interpreted not as leverage to be reciprocated but as elasticity to be tested repeatedly. Funnily, Trump continues to describe Modi as a friend while deploying every available statute and legislative opportunity to damage his prestige at home. The Trumpian presidency has been transformed from an institution that seeks to forge global consensus into one that thrives on confrontation. Leaders like Netanyahu and Zelenskyy, who postpone or avoid fresh electoral mandates, receive public support and diplomatic latitude. But the fastest-growing large democracy is treated as a problem to be managed through successive layers of tariffs.

Policies that generate worldwide economic instability fall with particular force on brown democracies that lack China’s strategic weight or Europe’s alliance insulation. Modi has so far kept his counsel and refused to escalate, preserving India’s strategic autonomy and room for manoeuvre. Yet, the longer this campaign of coercive diplomacy continues, the clearer it becomes that the damage will rebound upon Trump’s own political base and upon the American economy.

As India expands its manufacturing base, deepens partnerships across the Global South, and positions itself as a credible counterweight to Chinese influence in South Asia, it will emerge stronger, not weaker. By targeting that rising power, Washington is not protecting Americans. It is eroding the commercial relationships and strategic partnership that once promised to balance Asia and advance shared interests.

A superpower that mistakes harassment for statecraft will eventually discover that the countries it seeks to discipline possess alternatives, and that the voters who once cheered confrontation will tire of higher prices, disrupted supply chains and diminished alliances. India has already demonstrated the patience of a rising power that knows time is on its side. America would do well to remember that patience is not the same as permanent forbearance, and that the weaponisation of diplomacy ultimately weakens the hand that wields it.

text:
I just helped a random guy dig sand crabs out from under the sand for fishing bait.
He was walking under the Washington Pier with a net, so I asked what he was doing.

“Catching sand crabs.” So naturally… I started catching sand crabs too. Caught a bunch of big ones. 

He looked a little confused about who I was. Probably thought I was a cop. Nope. Just a random sand crab catcher, one who caught more than him I might add. 

I call these little moments “Strangers & Freaks,” after the GTA V missions.

Every now and then I’ll ask random people what they’re up to, offer to help, or just ask if I can tag along for a bit.

Sometimes you’re posing against a wall because a couple that’s absolutely blitzed wants you in their Abbott Kinney photo shoot (they don’t have a camera).

Sometimes you’re helping a hungover woman dig her phone out from under the pier. 

Sometimes a group of models would rather ride with you to a bar than wait for an Uber  in a sketchy neighborhood.

And sometimes you follow a homeless guy to what he swears is evidence JFK was an alien, only to discover it’s a shopping cart full of junk.

Not every “Strangers & Freaks” mission has a fun ending. Most of them don’t. But they almost always make for a better story than sitting at home.

text:
advisory from a senior citizen visiting the US, facing unthinkable hardships after arriving from India.

We have been staying in Seattle, Washington, for the past two months. My wife was suffering from a severe respiratory issue when we left India. After using those medicines from India,here in the US, she had almost recovered.

However, as our supply ran out, So, I asked my daughter to schedule an appointment with a pulmonologist in Seattle.For that first we had to consult a general physician . 
We were given an appointment for a week later , only via a video call.

We spoke to the doctor on the phone for about 10 minutes.He said he  prescribed appropriate medicines, stating that we could pick them up from a pharmacy.
 The medicines were not immediately available and would take 4–5 days to arrive from India.

We finally received the medicines on the fifth day. The medicines were  labeled 'Made in India'. 
Even after a 50% discount through US medical insurance, we still had to pay an equivalent of ₹21,000. This means medicines costing just ₹2,500 in India cost a staggering ₹42,000 in the US.

It took us 12 days to obtain medicines here that are readily available at any pharmacy in India.
 A week later, we received a bill of $283 (approximately ₹23,000) for the doctor's consultation fee.

Consider yourselves to be fortunate to be living in India during your retirement years.

We often look abroad in search of a "good life." But if we pause to think... certain everyday conveniences—unavailable even to billionaires in London or New York—are easily accessible to the middle class in India.

Here are *7 examples* showing that even the life of a common person in our country is a **VIP lifestyle**:

*1 Data Democratization:*
While countries around the world spend over $50 (approx. ₹4,000) a month for basic internet, we enjoy high-speed 5G data for just ₹300. We have the cheapest data in the world! This is what has digitally transformed our economy.

*2 The "10-Minute" doorstep delivery:* 
Run out of ginger for your tea or out of milk? Place an order on Blinkit, Zepto, or Swiggy Instamart, and the item is in your hands before the water even boils. In Europe, by contrast, you’d have to put on a coat and walk 15 minutes in the cold to a store—and you wouldn't be surprised to find it already closed.

*3 Instant Healthcare:*
Need to see a specialist? You can go straight to the hospital. Need a blood test? A lab technician comes to your home as early as 6 AM to collect the sample, and the report arrives on your WhatsApp by afternoon. We don't face the three-month waiting lists or the nightmare of "insurance approvals" common elsewhere even for trivial ailments.

*4 Human Support System:*
Having people to help with house cleaning, cooking, and driving isn't a luxury reserved only for the wealthy here; it is the backbone of middle-class life. It offers something incredibly valuable: it saves **TIME**.

*5 The UPI Revolution:*
From a ₹5 roadside tea to a ₹50,000 laptop—everything is just a scan away! No need for wallets, no excuses like "the card machine isn't working," and absolutely no transaction fees. In this regard, the rest of the world lags far behind us.

*6 *"Free" Little Joys:*
No matter which restaurant you visit, you get a glass of drinking water for free (whereas elsewhere, they’d charge you $5). There’s an ironing man / chai wallah right at the end of the street to take care of our instant needs. It is these little things that make life run so smoothly.

*7 Social Bonds (Social Safety Net):*
We don't live in a culture of legal notices and courts; we live in a culture of relationships. If we face a problem, a neighbor won't send a court notice—they’ll lovingly cook and send over some *khichdi*.
*The Bottom Line:*

India is not merely a country; it is a wonderful world filled with conveniences at every turn.
Mera India Mahan

Washington State 

County Government Audit ☆ Internal Controls 

Washington State Auditor’s Office urge Lynnwood to strengthen internal controls after 2024 cyberfraud 

July 31, 2026

LYNNWOOD — A phishing scheme in 2024 led the City of Lynnwood to deposit $7,158 in payroll funds into a fraudulent bank account, exposing gaps in the city’s internal controls over electronic payments, according to a management letter from the Washington State Auditor’s Office.

The letter dated October 20, 2025, summarized issues identified during the accountability audit covering January 1 through December 31, 2024. The matters were not elevated to formal findings in the public audit report but were deemed significant enough to require attention from city management and the City Council. The letter was referenced in the audit report and is a public record.

Auditors found the city lacked adequate internal controls to protect public funds from internal and external threats involving electronic payments. The city reported the phishing incident in 2025. It involved a payroll payment redirected after a fraudulent request that appeared to change an employee’s bank account information.

☆ Since 2016, Washington local governments have reported more than $37 million in losses from cyberfraud schemes including phishing, spearphishing and business email compromises. In these schemes, external actors contact government staff while posing as known employees, managers, vendors or associates, then convince them to redirect legitimate payments or purchase gift cards.

The City of Lynnwood spent about $41.8 million on payroll in fiscal year 2024. Auditors examined controls over electronic payroll payments and identified three specific shortcomings:

The city’s policy requiring verification of bank change requests did not include all elements prescribed in the Budgeting, Accounting and Reporting System (BARS) Manual section 3.8.11.30;

Staff did not consistently or adequately follow the city’s intended procedures; 

and

Training was ineffective, with employees missing common red flags of phishing schemes.

The BARS Manual requires governments to adopt policies establishing effective internal controls for electronic funds transfers. These include bank-offered security measures to prevent unauthorized transfers, separate user IDs for those initiating or approving transactions, secure processes for creating and authenticating direct-deposit files, and validation of payment authorizations.

State auditors recommended that Lynnwood develop written policies and procedures for electronic payroll payments that incorporate the required BARS elements. The policies is to avoid reliance on information received through email, a medium traditionally vulnerable to unauthorized access. Auditors also urged the city to provide adequate communication and training, so staff can consistently follow verification requirements.

The management letter stated it is intended for the information and use of management and the governing body as recommendations to strengthen internal controls. Auditors said they look forward to reviewing the status of these matters in the city’s next audit.

The letter was disclosed in the City’s Finance Committee meeting on July 21, in connection with a broader financial review that identified underreported deficiencies and processes contributing to an additional $2.2 million budget deficit for 2026 than that was previously reported.

City officials have indicated they are revising internal processes and will work on the improvements.

WPATH FILES: Trans Org Wants Female Inmates To Overcome ‘Transphobia’ And Share Prisons With Men | Megan Brock, Daily Wire

The World Professional Association of Transgender Health (WPATH) is the world’s preeminent transgender medical organization and a leading force in the push for minors to receive transgender medical interventions, including sex-change surgeries. The group’s medical guidance, called the Standards of Care Version 8, informs clinical practice, insurance policy, and government regulations throughout the United States.

Systematic reviews and legal investigation have shown the SOC-8 to be built on faulty methodology and politicized science. The Federal Trade Commission filed a lawsuit against WPATH in June 2026, stating the organization has “misled parents and children about the medical consensus and medical necessity, as well as the safety and effectiveness” of child sex-change interventions.

WPATH members receive access to a member-only forum that discusses various topics related to transgender medicine and policy. Through a public records request The Daily Wire uncovered almost 250 pages of messages from WPATH’s member-only forum written between June 2024 and November 2024. The messages offer a glimpse into the organization’s cultural reach and challenge some of its public-facing recommendations.

This is the third article in The Daily Wire’s investigative series on the uncovered WPATH messages.

*

World Professional Association of Transgender Health (WPATH) members discussed how to help female inmates overcome “internalized transphobia” and learn to affirm “transgender” men living in women’s prisons.

Michelle Webb, a gender affirming program administrator for the Washington State Department of Corrections, suggested female inmates have “open and frank” discussions with “trained staff” to better understand the needs of men wanting to “live their authentic lives” in women’s prisons, messages from the WPATH online member forum show.

“The cis female population should have open and frank discussions with trained staff, with community experts, to understand why the [transgender and gender diverse] females want to be in an affirmative environment,” wrote Webb in the online forum. “They [are] not trying to take resources; they are not getting ‘more than’ cis females, they are just looking to live their authentic lives and have equity.”

Webb explained many men had a difficult time integrating into women’s prison and were “not accepted by the cis females.”

“[Transgender and gender diverse] females living in the cis female facilities have all mentioned something they call the ‘mask’ meaning the mask they wore in the male facilities, the mask that kept them safe, it allowed them to blend in and not draw attention to themselves,” wrote Webb. “When individuals were moved to the female facilities, they found it difficult to drop the mask and this made their integration into the female facilities extremely difficult, they were often not accepted by the cis females and on occasion were ostracized.”

WPATH’s medical guidance, the Standards of Care Version 8, has been cited in multiple lawsuits demanding prison systems implement policies that affirm gender ideology and provide “gender-affirming” healthcare.

Amie Ichikawa, an ambassador at Independent Women and co-founder of the nonprofit Woman II Woman , told The Daily Wire transgender activists have treated female inmates as “support animals,” forcing them to cater “to the fleeting feelings of male inmates who identify as women.”

“Departments of Corrections across the country have let WPATH bully them into sacrificing female prisoners to be used like support animals,” Ichikawa said. “Never, at any point, should a woman need to be reprogrammed to accommodate a male inmate. This is just a peek into the female future if we do not stop this attack on their existence.”

Ichikawa says the effort to include men in women’s prison is making incarcerated women “invisible.”

“Prison is already a difficult place to be. The aggressive, forced acceptance of gender ideology as some kind of state-sanctioned religion has pushed incarcerated women completely out of the spectrum of concern,” Ichikawa told The Daily Wire. “They barely had any visibility or relevance before this started trending, so they are almost invisible now.”

The Daily Wire obtained the WPATH forum messages through a public record request to the Washington Department of Corrections, which has some of the most radical transgender prison policies in the nation. Washington State is being investigated by the Department of Justice for forcing women to be housed with men, in possible violation of their constitutional right to safe incarceration. The America First Policy Institute filed a lawsuit against the Washington Department of Corrections in April 2026 that alleges two women living in a Washington State Women’s prison were assaulted by a “six-foot-four, ‘biologically intact’ male” with a history of violence against women, housed in a women’s prison because he self-identifies as female.

Leigh Ann O’Neill, America First’s chief legal affairs officer, told The Daily Wire women should be able to rely on corrections staff to prioritize their physical safety over the feelings of men.

“While women incarcerated in state prisons should be able to rely on corrections officials to protect their physical safety and support their rehabilitation, these officials were instead coordinating with WPATH over ways to make male inmates feel more comfortable in women’s prisons,” O’Neill said.

“These emails raise serious questions about the influence WPATH has exerted over correctional policies affecting some of the most vulnerable women in government custody,” she added. “Female inmates should never be treated as collateral damage in the pursuit of an ideological agenda. Department of Corrections has a legal and moral duty to protect the women in their custody from foreseeable physical and sexual harm — not to prioritize the comfort of male inmates over the safety, dignity, and rights of women.”

Webb’s comments were in response to a post by a psychologist who asked WPATH members what skills “transgender” males needed to learn to adapt to life in women’s prisons and find “joy in their identities,” records show.

“I am still trying to identify all the things transgender women need to know about being in a female facility versus what they learned in a male facility,” wrote the psychologist. “I am open to ideas that folks have, things they have heard from women about what they learned about how to do time in a women’s facility.”

The psychologist said they were designing a transgender integration unit to help men adapt to life in a women’s prison for the Colorado Department of Corrections, writing that “cultural forces” worked against men trying to integrate into women’s prison.

“There are structural and cultural forces acting against their individual success,” the psychologist wrote. “We can train staff all we want but the larger culture and social beliefs impact how custody staff behave. There are cultural issues that transgender women will have to face no matter how much we train the staff or other incarcerated people.”

The Colorado transgender integration unit was created as part of a settlement from a class action lawsuit filed by transgender inmates who claimed they faced discrimination in Colorado prisons.

The Washington Department of Corrections did not respond to The Daily Wire’s request for comment.

text:
the babies were each given two mothers. one was built of bare wire and held the milk. the other was wrapped in cloth and had nothing to offer at all. every one of them chose the cloth, and crossed to the wire one only when hunger got bad enough, and then hurried back…

the year was 1958. the man running it was harry harlow at the university of wisconsin, and the infants were rhesus macaques taken from their mothers within hours of birth.

the accepted theory then even had a name. cupboard love. affection was understood as a byproduct of feeding: the infant attaches to the mother because the mother is where the food is, and the rest is sentiment.

harlow built the two surrogates to test it. a wire frame with a bottle, and a wire frame wrapped in terry cloth with no bottle. half the infants were fed by the wire mother, half by the cloth.

which one fed them turned out not to matter. they spent up to eighteen hours a day on the cloth and went to the wire only to eat. when he frightened them, every one of them ran to the cloth, including the infants it had never fed once. they would grab hold of it, and then, still holding on, turn around and face the thing that scared them.

he titled the address he gave that year "the nature of love."

the work was cruel and he knew it. the isolation studies that came after are among the most disturbing in the history of the field. what they bought was the end of a hospital era in which sick children were kept clean, fed, and almost never held, because holding them was thought to be medically pointless.

this week the chief executive of openai suggested parents connect the family calendar to a chatbot so it can produce a personalized podcast for the drive to school. one kid's soccer game that afternoon. another kid's birthday coming up. some news.

the drive to school is twenty minutes in a closed box with nowhere else to be. no audience, no schedule until the door opens. it is one of the last places a kid will tell you something sideways, staring out the window, that they would never say across a dinner table. the podcast fills that silence with content about their own life, produced overnight, narrated by no one.

harlow's monkeys had every need the wire could meter, and they still spent eighteen hours a day holding the mother who gave them nothing but herself. the finding was never that food doesn't matter. the finding was that presence is not a delivery mechanism, and the infants knew the difference before anyone could teach it to them.

everything a child needs, on schedule, from the wire. everything except the reason they hold on.

On 5 June 1967, thanks to this intelligence, Israel launches a surprise strike. The Egyptian air force is destroyed on the ground. In six days, Israel takes Gaza, Sinai, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan.

General Shlomo Gazit would admit: “We knew they were not ready. This information gave us the certainty that we could win.”
Out of mistrust toward his Arab neighbors, King Hassan II offered Israel a decisive advantage. Without Morocco, the Six-Day War might have had a completely different outcome.

Bentley Shelton (2027 Guard) put together an impressive summer on the New Balance P32 Circuit, emerging as one of Darius Garland Elite’s @DGEliteNB most versatile and dependable players. Competing against some of the nation’s top talent, Shelton consistently showcased his ability to impact the game on both ends of the floor, proving he could defend multiple positions while expanding his offensive arsenal. His strong play throughout the live periods has continued to generate momentum on the recruiting trail. Shelton now holds a multitude of Division I offers, including a recent offer from Air Force, while several other programs continue to show strong interest. With a number of major campus visits on the horizon, his recruitment is only continuing to trend upward.

Former NBA player Winston Garland praised Shelton’s growth while also highlighting the continued rise of Darius Garland Elite on the New Balance P32 Circuit. “Bentley had a great summer with us. He showed he could play multiple positions. This was our third year in the New Balance league, and it’s been good. Darius Garland is putting his resources into it and helping build the program.” Program director Antwon Brown echoed those sentiments, saying, “The season went well. This was our third year on the New Balance P32 Circuit, and we’ve really picked things up. There are a lot of good teams, especially at the top. Having Bentley was refreshing. He’s a great teammate who knows how to play the game the right way, whether he’s on or off the ball. He developed throughout the season.”

Shelton believes the summer gave him the opportunity to demonstrate the complete evolution of his game. “I felt like I was able to stand out and show how much I’ve developed,” Shelton said. “I showed I can shoot off the dribble, handle the ball, and play positions one through four. Being a versatile defender was something I wanted to prove, and I felt like I did that throughout the events.” Looking ahead, Shelton plans to play with the YNG Dreamerz @yngdreamerz in Overtime Elite @OvertimeElite , where he hopes to continue showing the growth in his game. “I want to keep showing how my game is developing,” Shelton said.

Having evaluated Shelton over the past several years, I’ve watched him grow from a knockdown shooter into a much more complete player. With good size for a shooting guard, positional versatility, and a continually expanding skill set, Shelton has established himself as an intriguing Division I prospect with his best basketball still ahead of him.

The best areas of the Alabama coast in November are Gulf Shores, Orange Beach, and Fort Morgan, offering daytime highs in the mid-60s to low 70s°F, low humidity, and very small crowds. [1, 2]

Area Breakdown for November
•Gulf Shores (Central): Best for convenience and outdoor access. It puts you right next to Gulf State Park, which features 28 miles of paved biking trails and cooler-weather nature walks. [1, 2]
•
•Orange Beach (East): Best for a relaxed, resort-style stay. Areas like Romar Beach offer quiet stretches of sand close to great local dining without the high-traffic summer noise. [1, 2, 3]
•
•Fort Morgan (West): Best for absolute solitude. Located on a secluded peninsula west of Gulf Shores, its uncrowded shorelines are ideal for peaceful beach walks and bird watching. [1, 2, 3]
•

November Travel Tips
•Weather: Expect daytime temperatures around 62°F to 72°F and chilly evenings dropping into the 50s°F.
•
•Swimming: Water temperatures dip to around 65°F, which is too cold for most casual swimmers, making rentals with heated indoor or outdoor pools a priority. [1, 2, 3, 4]

text:
Tracy Grant:
"Dear Scorps, and family and friends of Scorps,
"On Wednesday, July 22, 2026, every trace of content I had posted on Facebook since 2009 vanished without warning. Based on what I’ve been able to piece together, it appears that someone gained access to my business Facebook Page and carried out actions so severe that Facebook permanently suspended my entire account.
"The account I’m writing from now was created in 2017 as a backup admin for the Scorps in Heaven group. At the time, I was producing such a high volume of files and posts for the group that Facebook temporarily restricted my activity for posting too much, too quickly. Having a second account allowed me to continue managing the group even when those temporary suspensions occurred. It’s the only thing I ever used this account for.
"In 2014, while our class was preparing for our 40th reunion, I was one of the people helping track down classmates.
"As I worked through the list, I began compiling the names of those who had passed away. Seeing those names gathered together, I felt an overwhelming sense that simply listing them wasn’t enough — I needed to see their faces again.
"One face in particular stayed with me: my friend, Ceil Lee. When I first joined Facebook in 2009, she was one of the people I most hoped to reconnect with, only to learn she had passed away in 2006. That loss made the project feel even more personal. Remembering her, and all the others, is what compelled me to go back to my yearbook and bring their faces forward again.
So I scanned each person’s photograph, and created an individual memorial for every classmate we had lost. I then assembled the memorials into an album within our group so everyone in our class could share in remembering them.
"One day, while we were still searching for classmates, a fellow classmate asked me to post the list of names for our class in the Scorps in Heaven group. At the time, the group had around 300 members. There was a single shared file that anyone could edit, and the idea was simple: whenever someone learned that a Scorp had passed away, they added the name to the list. So I went to that file and, under my class year, added a neatly organized list that included each person’s name, date of birth, and date of death.
"As I looked around the group, I noticed that a photo album had been created for each graduating class, but most of them were empty. Since I had already made the memorials for my own class, I simply uploaded them into the designated album.
"In 2015, I had just finished a complete overhaul of my business website — months of grueling sixteen hour days that left me exhausted and honestly sick of looking at it. Around that time, I found myself revisiting the list of names in the Scorps in Heaven group, and I felt moved to start learning more about each person we had lost.
Quietly, I began creating memorials and posting them in the appropriate class albums. To make the tributes more complete, I purchased yearbooks on eBay so I could access senior photos, and I borrowed additional yearbooks from others to scan the pages myself. As I worked, I also started cleaning up the shared list — correcting classmates who had been placed in the wrong year and removing names of people who were, thankfully, still alive.
"Another issue that emerged was that people were posting freely in the discussion. As a result, some individuals received several posts, while others received none at all. It quickly became clear that the only way to ensure everyone was properly recognized was to turn off open posting and create a single memorial post for each person, where all comments could be gathered in one place.
"Someone eventually shared a spreadsheet with me that supposedly contained the names of all alumni. It was riddled with errors, but over the years I’ve gradually corrected and refined it. What began as a simple task turned into a long-term effort to honor our classmates with accuracy, care, and respect.
"To keep better track of everyone — and to understand how families were connected across different graduating classes — I created the SHS Families tree on Ancestry. For each memorial I made, I added an image of it to the tree, allowing the tributes to live not only within the Facebook groups but also within a structured, searchable family history.
"Over time, the number of memorials grew from the thirty or so I had created for my own class to more than 2,250. The Scorps in Heaven group itself expanded to over 5,500 members. For the classes that allowed me to join their individual groups, I posted memorials there as well, making sure each class could honor its own.
"Because Scorps in Heaven was meant to be a solemn space, I also saw the need for a place where people could share lighter memories and reconnect more freely. That’s why I created the Satellite High Memories group — a companion space where stories, photos, and everyday nostalgia could live alongside the memorials.
"All of that is now gone.
"When I was a little girl, my father would sometimes grow exasperated with me and exclaim, “Tracy! Why do you have to make a big production out of everything?” Years later, when I was a young adult working as a legal secretary in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, Martin Ray — the attorney I worked for — said the very same thing: “Tracy! Why do you have to make a big production out of everything?”
"Over time, I’ve come to understand that this isn’t a flaw or a quirk. It’s simply who I am. I create “big productions” because I want things to be meaningful. I want them to bring joy, comfort, and connection to people. It’s my way of honoring others and making the world a little brighter.
"I’m sharing all of this because I want my fellow Scorps to understand that my “big production” was never one grand gesture — it was the result of thousands of small, careful acts over many years. I never wanted, expected, or sought recognition. My joy has always come from the quiet stories people have shared with me about what a single memorial meant to them. It comes from knowing that these efforts helped people reconnect with old friends, and even form new friendships. That has always been the true reward.
"From the very beginning of this fiasco, I understood that the solution was not to fight to have my Facebook account restored. In my eyes, Facebook is actually the ultimate victim here. Thousands of pages I built — each one generating activity, engagement, and ad traffic — are now gone from their platform. But the memories, the connections, and the friendships forged through all of that work still live on in all of you.
"I’ve already spent more than two years battling Facebook’s system to recover five class albums that their algorithm deleted, likely because they contained links to obituary sites Facebook didn’t approve of. After endless appeals and dead ends, I finally gave up and spent months reconstructing those albums myself. I won’t be fooled again into pouring my time and energy into fighting with a machine to reclaim what I created.
"Facebook offers no customer service. There is no human being to speak to, no one who understands context or intention. Everything is governed by AI and algorithms — and when something goes wrong, there is simply no path back. I refuse to spend my life wrestling with a system that cannot see the humanity behind what was lost.
"Yes, I know there are organizations that claim they can restore my account for a fee. To me, that feels like paying extortion. I also understand that once my profile was reinstated, I could pay $15 a month for a verified account. To me, that feels like blackmail. I won’t do either.
"No — the only real solution, if there is to be one, is to create a standalone site. But a site that simply houses the memorials wouldn’t be enough to keep people engaged. What’s the point of preserving all that work if no one visits it?
"To truly matter, it would need to be more than an archive. It would have to function as a full alumni hub — something that combines the purpose of Scorps in Heaven with the spirit of Satellite High Memories, and also provides a place for each class to plan reunions. A living, active space where memorials, memories, and community can coexist.
"It would have to be a place that can’t be erased at the whim of an algorithm — a space whose existence isn’t dependent on automated decisions or opaque systems. It needs to be something durable, intentional, and human centered, where the work we’ve built and the memories we’ve preserved can’t simply disappear overnight.
"The thought of creating something that large feels overwhelming right now. I need time and space to recover, to breathe, and to decide whether what I’ve already built is enough — or whether I truly want to devote myself to a project of that magnitude. I am genuinely at peace with what has happened. I just need the time to reflect and determine what my next steps should be.
"Thank you for your concern, your patience, and your continued support. It means more than you know. Over the past week, your messages, your kindness, and even your quiet understanding have reminded me why I poured so much of myself into this community in the first place. Every note, every gesture, every expression of care has helped steady me.
"I want you to know that your support hasn’t just been comforting — it has been grounding. It has reminded me that the work I did mattered, not because of where it lived online, but because of the people it touched. And knowing that so many of you are still here, still connected, still carrying those memories forward, has made this difficult moment feel a little lighter.
"So truly — thank you. Your presence, your encouragement, and your faith in me mean far more than I can express in a single sentence."

text:
Sara Almosawi, 24, is a daughter of immigrants and, through one lens, an exemplar of the American dream. Her parents immigrated from Iraq and Indonesia, met in Alabama, and settled in Orlando, Fla. Her father drove a truck while her mother mostly worked restaurant jobs.

She landed at Cornell after the school offered her generous financial aid—a “golden ticket,” as she called it. Then came Oct. 7th during her first semester in upstate New York.

As at other universities, student protesters built an encampment. They expressed disbelief that mainstream Democrats hedged over whether to call Israel’s conduct in Gaza a “genocide.” 

The Democratic Socialists of America, with a long record of pro-Palestenian activism, was a natural vessel for those who joined the protests.

Once a baby boomer relic, the far-left DSA now counts more than 120,000 members, about half of whom joined since late 2024, after Israel’s war in Gaza ignited campus protests nationwide and energized young recruits like Almosawi. 

DSA national leaders like Almosawi scarcely hide their disdain for a Democratic Party they view less as a partner than a hostile takeover target. 

“Ultimately, the strategy of the DSA has been to primary mainstream Democrats. And we’re going to continue to do that,” she said on a recent afternoon as she sat in a Yemeni coffeehouse in Brooklyn. “We’re gonna take it over. We’re done with this. They’re not meeting the American people where they are.”

By late 2024, Almosawi faced her own reckoning. Cornell suspended her for disrupting a career fair that included defense contractors. Despite her parents’ misgivings, she has spent the past year nurturing YDSA chapters around the country while serving on the DSA’s national political committee.

“My intention was to graduate. But this is the most important time for socialism in America since the 1920s,” she said. “The iron is hot. The moment is now.”

Once a fringe wing, the DSA movement is wielding surprising political power, capitalizing on popular discontent. Mainstream Democrats see a "fundamental threat."

Farewell Climbers, May You Soar High! 🏔️ 🇵🇰 

We are heartbroken. 💔 
From the moment we received news of the avalanche of 30 July on Broad Peak, we held on to a fragile hope that a miracle might bring the team back safely. That hope faded leaving all of us in shreds, and we are left to accept the painful reality of this loss.

This is one of the heaviest losses we have faced in recent years. We lost three of our own climbers in the avalanche, and with them, ten mountaineers who shared a deep love for the Himalaya and the mountains.

Nature offers no soft corners. The high mountains remain inherently dangerous, and every climber who goes there understands the risks involved. From Nims Dai, a global figure in mountaineering, to the aspiring Yukta, and to our own Gyalu Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa, and Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, each of them was an experienced climber who knew the nature of the high peaks.

In the end, the mountains decide. We can only prepare as best as we can.

We offer our final farewell to the departed and pray that their families find the strength and courage to carry this profound grief.

Farewell, climbers.
May you soar high eternally.

CHROME
WebMCP Early PreviewAuthorsAlexandra Klepper
Andre Bandarra
Carlos Giraldo
François Beaufort
Contact●Questions & Feedback
●Bug reports
UpdatedFeb 10, 2026
Introduction
WebMCP is a proposed web standard that exposes structured tools for AI agents on existing websites. This would replace "screen-scraping" with robust, high-performance page interaction and knowledge retrieval. WebMCP provides JavaScript and annotates HTML form elements so that agentic browsers know exactly how to interact with page features to support a user's experience.

By exposing APIs to the browser agent, WebMCP significantly improves the performance and reliability of AI agent actuation.

The following are some examples of how WebMCP could be applied to your website: 

●Example Airline's website exposes a book_flight tool. Agents use this tool to submit structured passenger data directly, rather than guessing how data should be input, based on Example Airline's calendar UI which is designed for human users.
●Complex medical or legal portals annotate forms as a submit_application tool. The agent can map data to fields correctly and instantly, instead of repeating data in incorrect fields. For example, indicating a field requires a full legal name versus separate first and last name fields.
●A developer settings page exposes a run_diagnostics tool, so an agent can trigger fixes that are otherwise hidden behind nested menus.
Purpose
WebMCP bridges the gap between web applications and AI agents by providing a contract for interaction. Rather than the agent guessing the purpose of a button or the structure of a form, the website can explicitly publish its interface. This contract defines:

●Discovery: A standard way for agents to query exactly which tools a page supports, such as checkout or filter_results.
●JSON Schemas: Explicit definitions of inputs and expected outputs, to reduce hallucination or misunderstanding.
●State: A shared understanding of the current page context, so the agent knows what resources are available to act on in real time.
Early preview goals
Our goal for the WebMCP early preview is to understand the following topics:

●Use cases: Identify when you think you'd use WebMCP and how it supports a given task.
●API shape and usability: Feedback on the ergonomics of the WebMCP APIs. Are there functions you expect to find in the APIs that don't yet exist?
●Tooling ecosystem: Debugging, testing, and verifying tool definitions with evaluations (evals).
●Implementation issues: Bugs or friction points in the Chrome implementation. Please note that this is an early preview - there will likely be bugs and points of friction, and we’re hoping you’ll help us find them.

We are seeking your feedback to shape our understanding.
Availability
WebMCP is available behind a flag  in Chrome 146. Learn more about Chrome flags.
Requirements
To use WebMCP, you need:
●Chrome: Version 146.0.7672.0 or higher.
●Flags: The "WebMCP for testing" flag must be enabled.

Imperative API
Use the Imperative API to define tools, using standard JavaScript.
registerTool
Use registerTool to add a single tool to the existing set without removing others.

window.navigator.modelContext.registerTool({
  name: "addTodo",
  description: "Add a new item to the todo list",
  inputSchema: {
    type: "object",
    properties: {
      text: { type: "string" }
    }
  },
  annotations: {
    readOnlyHint: "true"
  },
  execute: ({ text }) => {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Added todo: ${text}` }] };
  }
});


unregisterTool
Use unregisterTool to remove a specific tool by name.

window.navigator.modelContext.unregisterTool("addTodo");

provideContext

provideContext is a convenience wrapper to register multiple tools at once. It replaces the entire set of registered tools, so you can reset functionality when the application state changes significantly.
window.navigator.modelContext.provideContext({
  tools: [{
    name: "addTodo",
    description: "Add a new item to the todo list",
    inputSchema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: {
        text: { type: "string" }
      }
    },
    execute: ({ text }) => {
      return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Added todo: ${text}` }] };
    }
  }, {
    name: "markComplete",
    description: "Mark a todo item as complete",
    inputSchema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: {
        id: { type: "string" }
      }
    },
    execute: ({ id }) => {
      return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Marked ${id} as complete` }] };
    }
  }]
});

clearContext
Call clearContext() to remove the entire set of tools at once.  

window.navigator.modelContext.clearContext()
